The attribute is autocomplete="garbage", an invalid token used to switch off browser autofill, which is why axe flags it; no assistive technology is told a wrong purpose. 4.1.2 passes: the probe shows role combobox, name frequency, expanded and haspopup states. 3.3.2 passes: the field has a visible Repeat label and a name. No other A or AA criterion concerns the token.

The sweep's walk stopped at stop 52 because one Tab press after the Accounts combobox drops focus to body; the next Tab continues to the table checkboxes.

Both sampled buttons are icon-only overflow menus with no name: the tree gives button "" [expanded=false, haspopup=menu]. The row menu on accounts.statements is the only path to the QuickBooks CSV and NetSuite CSV exports, and the Invoicing card menu on home is the only path to Invoice settings and Hide from Home, so 4.1.2 fails. It is not a form control or the sole primary action, and the task stays possible, so it stays medium.

The Accounts listbox opens as soon as Tab lands on the combobox (aria-expanded goes true and the 280px list shows), so by the time Enter or Space is pressed it is already open. Arrow keys move through the options and Space or Enter toggles one, which changed the table to include Credit, so the filter works from the keyboard.

The sweep pressed Enter and Space on the tab-stop wrapper div around the Transfer split button, which has no action. The real trigger is the Open Menu chevron button, the third Tab stop in the group: on both states Tab reaches it, and Enter and Space each open the Transfer in / Transfer out menu, move focus into it and Escape returns focus to the chevron.

The September net return row on Treasury is a plain div with a click handler: no role, no tabindex, no focusable child. Tab walks 62 stops and passes from the allocation card to the Oct 2 transfer row without stopping on it (shot:a11y/runs/2026-10-03-1525/shots/verify/verify-053/accounts.treasury-net-return-row-skipped-by-tab.png). That row is the only control I found that opens the September 2026 net return dialog, which shows the MCRYX and MRGXX dividends and the Treasury fee behind the figure, so a keyboard user cannot reach the breakdown and no equivalent keyboard path exists.

The dl holds div wrappers that each contain a dt and a plain div standing in for the dd (the markup carries an as="dd" attribute on a div), so the list exposes terms with no definitions (ax probe: DescriptionList with no name). The label and amount of each line still read in order, so the pairing survives in reading order and the impact is small, but 1.3.1 is not met.

On both states the link is regular-weight text in #465bd1 inside body text in #363644, with no underline, border or other cue (computed text-decoration: none), and the pair measures 2.08:1 where 1.4.1 needs 3:1 without a cue. The two contrast probes pass at 5.06:1 and 5.71:1, but they measure each link against its background, which is a different pair, so they do not answer this finding. Neither link is essential text (a footnote link, and an inline reset that duplicates the Reset buttons on the same screen), and 2.08:1 is not under 2:1, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order needs a sequence that preserves meaning and operability: the fund card is a description column and a data column side by side, and focus walks one column and then the other, in DOM order. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence is met for the same reason. No stop is skipped, and focus does not change context, so 3.2.1 is not engaged.
reason: The rise is the move from the Prospectus link at the bottom of the left column of the first fund card (y 665) to the Net Yield info icon in its right-hand data column (y 551, no scroll in between). Focus finishes the description column, then goes through the data column, which is how the card reads. Both stops are reachable and operable.

Tab goes from the info icon in the second fund card's data column to the here. footnote link below it, which is forward in the page (document y 907 to 992 in my Tab walk). The scroll container moved about 250px between the two stops (scrollTop 27 to 273), so the focus ring's viewport y fell from 880 to 719, the sweep's numbers, which I reproduced. The sweep compared viewport rects across that scroll.

The Mercury logo link to /redirect has an SVG wordmark with no title, aria-label or text, so the tree exposes link with an empty name and it fails 4.1.2 and 2.4.4. It is a secondary home shortcut: View loan details and Make Another Request carry the visible next steps, so the task is not blocked and the impact is minor.

The confirmation You've requested $250,000 USD from your Venture Debt loan replaces the form in place on the same URL, outside any live region: the page's only role=alert node is the empty toast container, focus drops to body, the title is unchanged and the page has no heading. It is the only confirmation of a money movement, so a screen-reader user hears nothing after submitting.

Request amount may not exceed $1,000,000.00. sits in a plain div with no live ancestor (the page's only role=alert node is empty) while focus stays in the amount field. The field has aria-errormessage but no aria-invalid, so the tree exposes no invalid state or message either. A screen-reader user who submits 2,000,000 hears nothing and has to explore the page to learn why; the task is possible, and this is an error, not the confirmation of a money movement.

On billpay.accounting-settings, Tab goes from Add to bookmarks to Edit and skips the three view tabs. On both sampled states the tabs are plain divs with tabindex -1 and no role, so the Categorization rules and Automation settings views open only on a mouse click. No link on either screen points to /categorization-rules or /automation-settings, so a keyboard user cannot reach those two views and cannot create rules or change automation, which makes it high.

On both sampled states the file input is an unlabeled, near-invisible input that Tab reaches and the tree exposes as button "Choose File", the browser's default text. The visible text (Drag and drop here or click to upload, You may upload one CSV file or JPEG or PNG file) is not tied to the input, so 4.1.2 still fails, but the control has a name and does what it says, the unnamed dialog aside, so a screen-reader user can still pick a file: low.

value.template: textbox "<amount>" [invalid=true, errormessage=Must be a dollar value.]

reason: The amount input has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at the visible 'Must be a dollar value.' span, and the accessibility tree exposes that message on the field. The span is not in a live region and not in aria-describedby (which points to a missing helptext id), so the message is not announced when it appears, but a screen-reader user who focuses the field still gets it. 4.1.2 weakly fails, with minor impact.

On the edit panel, the Invoice date input is announced as textbox "Select due date", the same name as the Due date input above it, so its visible label Invoice date is not in its accessible name (2.5.3). The amount input is named only by its 0.00 placeholder. A screen-reader user still hears the labelled button Invoice date Apr 18, 2025 just before the input and the field announces its current date, so this is friction, not a blocker.

The Invoice no. input (value INV-902) has no accessible name on both sampled states: the AX tree shows textbox with an empty name, no label, aria-label or placeholder. It is an unnamed form control, which the guidance rates high, but the button Invoice no. INV-902 precedes it in tab order and says what the field is, and the field is secondary to paying the bill, so the task is possible but hard: medium.

The Invoice date Apr 18, 2025 button contains a text input: the AX tree shows button > textbox "Select due date" on both states, and Tab stops on the button and then on the input. A button's children are presentational, so assistive technology may not expose the nested input reliably (4.1.2). The guidance gives no reason to lower it, so it stays medium.

The Due date Apr 19, 2025 button contains a text input: the AX tree shows button > textbox "Select due date" on both states. Enter on the outer button does nothing and leaves focus on it, so it is a dead tab stop in front of the real control, and the nesting fails 4.1.2. The guidance gives no reason to lower it, so it stays medium.

The Invoice no. INV-902 button contains a text input: the AX tree shows button > unnamed textbox on both states, and Tab stops on the button and then on the input. The nesting fails 4.1.2 and the input's only label sits on the outer button. The guidance gives no reason to lower it, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 covers messages that report success, results, state or errors. The flagged node wraps the Done control, whose name is Done; a control label is not a status message, and the confirmation itself (Thanks for your feedback and the body text) is covered by separate findings. 4.1.2 passes: the inner button has the role button and the name Done. 2.4.3 and 3.3.x are not part of this claim and nothing else about the label fails an A or AA criterion.
reason: The flagged node is the wrapper around the Done button, which the accessibility tree ignores; the button itself is exposed as button "Done" and is focusable. A button label is a control, not a status message, and the success message is the title and body text, which have their own findings.

The Thanks for your feedback title appears in the feedback panel after sending. The panel and the title have no live region, alert or status role in their ancestors, the page's existing role=status and role=alert regions stay empty, and focus is on the page body, so a screen reader announces nothing. The feedback is not a money movement, so it stays medium.

The follow-up text (We'll share your thoughts with our product teams...) appears in the same panel with no live region, alert or status role in its ancestors, the page's existing status and alert regions stay empty, and focus is on the body. A screen reader user gets no confirmation that the feedback was sent. The feedback is not a money movement, so it stays medium.

The filter toolbar is role=menubar but holds a menuitem chip plus two plain buttons (Remove filter, Reset), so it still fails 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 for required children. Tab reaches the chip, Remove filter and Reset in order and each one works, so keyboard and screen-reader users can still clear the filter and the harm is a misleading menubar announcement.

The pill is button "my-company-name@ap.mercury.com" and Enter on it does activate it: a click fires and the Copied tooltip appears on the next painted frame, with a visible focus ring. A DOM read taken right after Enter still shows nothing, which likely explains the sweep's reading. Space does nothing, but Enter is a working keyboard path, so the control is not mouse-only.

The select-all checkbox in the Documents & Data table header exposes as checkbox "" [checked=mixed] on both sampled states. It has no label, aria-label or title; the Account header text sits in another cell and is not tied to it, so 4.1.2 fails. The table is still readable and the rows can be selected, so it stays medium.

The 32px avatar button in the page header (aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded=false) is announced as button "" on both sampled states: it holds only an img with alt="" and has no aria-label or text, so 4.1.2 fails. The menu opens by keyboard, but nobody can tell the button opens the account menu; the sidebar Profile link covers part of what it offers, so it stays medium.

The checked row checkbox for Ops / Payroll exposes as checkbox "" [checked=true] on both sampled states. It sits inside a label with no text (input.labels is one empty label) and the account name is in the next cell, so 4.1.2 fails. Table navigation still shows the row, so the task is possible but hard: medium.

The download icon in the Ops / Payroll row is a link to a PDF (target=_blank) whose only content is an aria-hidden SVG, so it is announced as link "" on both sampled states and fails 4.1.2 and 2.4.4. The bottom Download button does the same for selected rows, but it depends on the unnamed checkboxes, so there is no clean equivalent: medium.

On accounts.bank-letters the AP row checkbox exposes as checkbox "" [checked=false] inside an empty label. On payments.ach-flagged the select-all checkbox in the Flagged table header exposes the same way, with input.labels empty. 4.1.2 fails on both; the tables can still be read cell by cell, so medium.

Toggle Private Mode is a toggle with no aria-pressed or aria-checked. I pressed Space on it: the icon changed from eye-slash to eye and localStorage privateMode went from disabled to enabled, while the name stayed Toggle Private Mode with no exposed state (shot:a11y/runs/2026-10-03-1525/shots/verify/verify-402/accounts.bank-letters-private-toggled.png). The on or off state shows only in the icon and the hover tooltip, so 4.1.2 fails; the button works and its effect shows in the amounts, so medium. I pressed Space again to restore it.

On both sampled states the page's only View all link announces as link View all. Its title, Recent transactions, is a span beside the link, not a heading, and shares no sentence, list item or table cell with it, so the purpose is not available as programmatic link context and 2.4.4 fails. The title comes right before the link in reading order and the link opens the account's transactions, so the impact is minor.

On both sampled states the eye icon button beside the Account number label has no text, aria-label or title and its SVG is aria-hidden, so it announces as button with no name. Pressing Enter on it reveals the full account number (3631271038) and swaps the icon to eye-slash with no name or state change announced. It is the only way to read the full number here, but it is focusable and sits right after its label, so the task is hard, not blocked.

On both sampled states the available balance is a link whose only text is the amount, $2,023,267.12, and the Available label beside it is not in the same sentence, list item or cell, so the link's purpose cannot be read from its text or programmatic context and 2.4.4 fails. It opens the account's transactions, the same URL as the View all link and the Transactions nav item, so another labeled link reaches the same place and the impact is minor.

On both sampled states the info icon in the Cashback earned column header is a link to mercury.com/legal/cashback-disclosure (opens a new tab) with no text, aria-label or title, an aria-hidden SVG and no aria-describedby, so it announces as link with no name and fails 4.1.2 and 2.4.4. It is the only way to the cashback terms and no other control carries the same destination, but the Cashback earned header gives some context and the link is focusable, so the task is hard, not blocked.

In the Linked accounts dialog the bank-icon link beside Exclude all accounts (to /accounts#external-accounts) has no text, aria-label or title, its SVG is aria-hidden and it has no aria-describedby, so it announces as link with no name and fails 4.1.2 and 2.4.4. Hovering shows a Go to Accounts tooltip, but Tab onto the link shows none, so keyboard and screen-reader users get no hint of where it goes; the task is hard, not blocked.

The All filter chip is a button with role=menuitem inside a role=menubar, and no aria-checked, aria-pressed or aria-current. Its on/off state shows only as a tinted background (shot:a11y/runs/2026-10-03-1525/shots/verify/verify-412/accounts.safes-filter-chips.png), so the tree reports menuitem "All" with no state on every sampled state. Arrow keys do not move between chips, so the menubar pattern is not implemented either. A screen-reader user cannot tell which SAFE filter is applied, and the filter persists in the URL, so the table can be filtered without them knowing. 4.1.2 fails; the task is possible but hard, so medium.

The 28px page title "Savings ••7658" is a read-only textarea labelled Add account nickname, so the tree reports textbox "Add account nickname" [readonly] (probe-a931bb1f4305), and the page has no heading elements at all (shot:a11y/runs/2026-10-03-1525/shots/verify/verify-413/accounts.savings-detail-nickname.png). The combobox that opens it is named Recipient emails and keeps focus while the list is open, so the control is still identifiable and only the popup's name is wrong: low.

The Email sent success overlay is a modal role=dialog with no aria-label or aria-labelledby, so the tree reports dialog "" on both states (probe-43b4cb5cc268, probe-46d66910d1f3) and 4.1.2 fails. The dialog takes focus and its first content is a visible h1 reading Email sent, so a screen-reader user still gets the title by reading on and can finish the task: low. The xpath is div[11] on the live page, not the div[12] the sweep recorded, because a portal count differs; the element matches by role and its 1440x718 rect.

The three-dot menu button at the end of each statement row, and the one on the Invoicing widget on Home, holds only an icon with aria-hidden, plus an empty visually-hidden label span, so the tree reports button "" [expanded=false, haspopup=menu] (probe-387ffccf0c02, probe-83b9a6e5ff5d). Enter opens it and it holds QuickBooks CSV and NetSuite CSV (shot:a11y/runs/2026-10-03-1525/shots/verify/verify-416/accounts.statements-menu-open.png), but a screen-reader user hears an unnamed button on every row and cannot tell what it opens. 4.1.2 fails. It is a secondary menu, not the sole primary action, and it can be operated, so the task is possible but hard: medium.

On both states the Transfer from button is a select-only combobox: role combobox, aria-haspopup=listbox, aria-expanded=false, the visible text Select an account as its value. Enter or Space on it sets aria-expanded=true, focus lands on the controlled listbox, and the options are exposed, so its role and state are correct and update. The listbox's own aria-labelledby points at a missing id, but that is a different element and not this finding's claim.

The Transfer to button is a select-only combobox on both states: role combobox, aria-haspopup=listbox, aria-expanded=false, the visible text Select an account as its value. On accounts.treasury-transfer-error, Enter sets aria-expanded=true and moves focus to the controlled listbox, so its role and state are correct and update; the payments state exposes the same markup. The listbox's own aria-labelledby points at a missing id, but that is a different element and not this finding's claim.

The Mercury logo link in the page header (href /redirect) holds only an SVG with no title, aria-label or text, so the tree exposes link with an empty name; the same holds on focus, where no tooltip or description appears. It fails 2.4.4 and 4.1.2, and no rule lowers it: the page's next steps are labelled, but a screen-reader user cannot tell where this link goes.

The Venture debt amount field's only accessible name is its placeholder, 0.00, on both states. The question How much do you want to borrow? is a plain div, not a label or heading, and nothing ties it to the input, so 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 fail (the listed 3.3.2 is met visually). A screen-reader user who tabs in hears 0.00 and not what the amount is for; the name does show a money amount and it is the step's only field, so the task is hard but possible: medium.

Tab stop 43 on the credit page is the tooltip-anchor wrapper div around the autopay control, and Enter and Space do nothing on it, which is what the sweep pressed. The very next stop (44) is the real button, and Enter on it opens the Autopay settings dialog with focus inside it. The button opens from the keyboard; the wrapper is only a redundant extra stop.

Reproduced: the Autopay settings dialog title is heading level 1 (the Credit Card page behind it is also level 1), while the Maintain a target account balance dialog title is level 3 and the only heading in its dialog. Dialog titles that look alike expose unrelated levels, so the heading hierarchy does not match the visual structure (1.3.1). Navigation and the task still work, so it stays low.

On both sampled states the file input is an unlabeled, near-invisible input that Tab reaches and the tree exposes as button "Choose File", the browser's default text. The visible text (Drag and drop here or click to upload, You may upload one CSV file or JPEG or PNG file) is not tied to the input, so 4.1.2 still fails, but the control has a name and does what it says, so a screen-reader user can still pick a file: low.

The Jason Green row is a table row with tabindex 0, and Tab reached it on the Needs Approval table. With the panel closed, Enter on the focused row opened the Approval request panel (the URL gained requestId and the panel showed on screen). Space does nothing, but Enter is enough for 2.1.1. Focus stays on the row instead of moving into the panel, which is a separate focus-order problem, not a mouse-only trigger.

The 0 of 2 label sits inside a tooltip anchor div with tabindex 0. With the mouse moved away (no tooltip, no role=tooltip in the DOM), Tab landed on that anchor, drew a focus ring and showed the Available Approvers tooltip with role=tooltip present. Focus shows what hover shows, so the tooltip is not hover-only.

On both sampled states, aria-expanded=false, aria-haspopup=menu and aria-controls sit on a role-less tabindex 0 div that wraps the Conversation history button, so axe is right that aria-expanded is not allowed there and the tree drops it. The inner button exposes no expanded or popup state, which weakens 4.1.2 a little; the menu still opens and the button has a name, so it is low.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in its Input Purposes list. Account type here is the checking or savings type of a recipient's bank account, so it is not information about the user and matches no listed purpose (cc-type is a card network, not an account type), and 1.3.5 does not apply even though the token is invalid. 4.1.2 is met: the combobox exposes name Account type, role combobox, expanded=false and haspopup=listbox, and the invalid token changes none of them. No other A or AA criterion covers an autocomplete token.
reason: On both sampled states the Account type combobox on the recipient form has autocomplete="garbage", an invalid token used on the form's recipient fields to suppress autofill. The field sets the payee's account type (placeholder Business Checking), so it collects nothing about the user and matches no listed input purpose, and the tree still exposes combobox Account type with its states.

The probe of the grey 30 in the due date calendar measures #9d9da8 on #ffffff at 2.68:1 for 14px text, where AA needs 4.5:1. The cell is not disabled (cursor pointer, pointer events on), so the inactive-component exception does not apply. It is the previous month's overflow day, not essential text for picking a date, so it stays above the high line and medium holds.

From billpay.bill-panel-edit, Tab stop 75 is the Due date button with no calendar in the DOM, and Tab stop 76 is the Select due date textbox, which opens the calendar on focus (the calendar day cells appear and the screenshot shows it). The sweep most likely pressed Enter and Space on a picker that focus had already opened. The trigger works from the keyboard.

The calendar's next-month chevron button (icon only, SVG hidden from the tree) is exposed as button with an empty name and is reachable by Tab, so it fails 4.1.2. The Select due date textbox is an editable text input with a name, so a date can be typed without the arrows, and the button is only a month-change aid: low. Its box also starts at x=1440, outside the 1440px viewport.

The calendar's previous-month chevron button (icon only, SVG hidden from the tree) is exposed as button with an empty name and is reachable by Tab, so it fails 4.1.2. The Select due date textbox is an editable text input with a name, so a date can be typed without the arrows, and the button is only a month-change aid: low.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard: the only function here is attaching a file, and the Upload attachment button does it from the keyboard (focus probes probe-ad25ce19dd63 and probe-d774db1a3a92: via tab, visible ring). The input is not a second function. 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap: trapped is false on both probes. 2.4.3 Focus Order: leaving an invisible duplicate out of the Tab sequence leaves no gap. 4.1.2 for the same input is covered by the name finding.
reason: The file input is an invisible duplicate (tabindex -1, opacity 1e-5, pointer-events none) stacked exactly over the Upload attachment button. Tab reaches that button on both states with a visible ring, and Enter and Space on it call the input's click(), so a keyboard user can attach a file.

The hidden file input has no label, so axe is right, and the tree exposes it as button "Choose Files", the browser's default text. It is an invisible duplicate (tabindex -1, opacity 1e-5, pointer-events none) of the visible Upload attachment button, which has a name, is reachable by Tab and does the same job. A screen-reader user can still attach a file, so 4.1.2 falls short with minor impact: low.

Both probes measure 2.68:1 (#9d9da8 on #ffffff, 15px) on the rule 6 text, Bank Description and Unknown GL Code, where AA needs 4.5:1. The dimmed row is not an inactive component: it has tabindex 0, no aria-disabled, and clicking it opens Rule details with Edit and Delete rule. The Invalid badge and the details panel stay readable, so the task is possible but harder, and the guidance line for high is not met.

Tab still reaches the Outcome select inside the closed Create categorization rule panel. The panel is aria-hidden with opacity 0, so focus lands on nothing visible (probe visible false, hidden invisible). The user can tab past it and finish, so it stays medium.

Tab reaches the Edit button inside the closed Rule details panel, which is aria-hidden with opacity 0 (probe visible false, hidden invisible), right after an equally invisible Delete rule button. Keyboard users get invisible stops but can tab past them, so it stays medium.
Tab reaches the Add condition button inside the closed Create categorization rule panel (aria-hidden, opacity 0): probe visible false, hidden invisible. The user can tab past it, so it stays medium.

On both states Tab lands on the Condition combobox while nothing shows focus. On the accounting page it sits in the closed aria-hidden panel (medium on its own). On books.rule-create the whole Create categorization rule form is at opacity 0 under reduced motion, so a keyboard user cannot see any field in a shared rule-builder panel and cannot create a rule. That makes it high.

On both states the first aside, Create categorization rule, has aria-hidden=true and opacity 0 yet holds 5 focusable controls (Close detail panel, Condition input, Add condition, selects), and Tab reaches them. The ax probe shows the node is ignored in the accessibility tree, so screen-reader users land on unannounced stops. It hides one closed panel, not the page, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the WCAG input-purpose list (name, email, address, card number and so on). The Condition 1 combobox picks which transaction field a categorization rule tests, so it has no listed purpose and 1.3.5 cannot fail. No other A or AA criterion covers an autocomplete token: 4.1.2 is met because the field exposes role combobox, name Condition 1 and expanded and haspopup states, and 4.1.1 is no longer in WCAG 2.2.
reason: The Condition 1 combobox has autocomplete="garbage" on both states, a deliberate way to keep browsers from autofilling it. It does not collect personal information, so no AA criterion fails, and the tree still exposes combobox "Condition 1" with its states.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 Status Messages covers information on the success, progress, waiting state or errors that follow an action. The error here is Must be a dollar value., which has its own finding. Flag error? is the text of a control that offers to report that error, so it is not a status message and 4.1.3 does not fail on it. No other criterion concerns announcing this text. Whether the badge, a pointer-only div with no role, is operable by keyboard is a different claim that this finding does not make.
reason: Flag error? is the label of a small badge beside the amount field that offers to report the validation error. It is a call to action, not information about the result of the user's action, so 4.1.3 does not cover it.

With the Recipient gets field empty, pressing Enter on Next shows Must be a dollar value. under the field while focus stays on Next. No live region or alert contains the message and the toast alert region never changes, so a screen-reader user hears nothing and the step does not advance. The field is marked invalid, so the user can find the cause by navigating back to it; the task is possible but hard.

The probe of the Flag error? badge measures 94 by 20 px with no clear 24 px circle, so 2.5.8 fails on height and spacing. The badge is a clickable target, not text in a sentence, and no equivalent control on the page meets 24 px, so no exception applies. It is a feedback affordance beside the field, not a money control, so it stays low.

On Pay bill's accounting step, with an empty line item added, pressing Enter on Next shows Please complete all fields while focus stays on Next. They can find the cause by exploring the form, so the task is possible but hard.

The probe reproduces 104x20 with offset 0, but the Create recipient button is the link-styled end of the sentence 'Adding someone new? Create recipient', and its height is set by the line of text it shares. That is the inline exception to 2.5.8.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order asks that focus order preserve meaning and operability. The order is banner buttons, then the sidebar nav ending at Settings, then the header and content, which keeps the meaning, and every control stays reachable. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence holds for the same reason: the DOM sequence matches the reading sequence of nav followed by content. The jump up the screen after the last nav link is the standard sidebar pattern, not a skipped control, so neither criterion fails.
reason: Tab does reach Finalize setup right after the Settings link, but Settings is the last link of the left sidebar nav and Finalize setup is the first control of the page header that follows the nav in the DOM. That is the usual nav-then-content order and it reads the same on both sampled states.

The gear button beside the Bill Pay email chip has no name, no title and no label, and activating it opens the Bill Pay settings dialog, so a screen reader announces "button" with no purpose. It fails 4.1.2 on both states. It is the way into that dialog but not a primary action, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.2 needs the name, role and state to be exposed and to match the control's behavior. On both states the chip exposes name Status, role menuitem with a menubar parent (a valid required parent), expanded flipping from false to true and haspopup=menu; Enter and Space open a role=menu popup, focus moves inside it, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the chip. 1.3.1 and 2.1.1 are met because the structure is valid and the keyboard works. A button with aria-haspopup would be the more usual choice, but that is a best practice, not an A or AA failure.
reason: The Status chip is a button with role menuitem inside a role=menubar toolbar, and it opens the role=menu popup named by aria-controls. Name, role, expanded and haspopup all match what it does, so the role is unconventional but not wrong.

The trash button on the first bill row takes Tab focus, but Enter and Space only open the row panel (Debug LLC with Review and Delete); the Delete item? dialog never opens, so 2.1.1 fails for this control. reason: Focus does land inside the menu, on the listbox Outcome, and the first ArrowDown sets aria-activedescendant to the first option, GL code, with a visible focus ring. Pressing Enter on the focused Status chip opens the menu with focus on its first item, the Overdue checkbox, and Tab steps to the next three. The sweep's check looks only for role=menuitem items, and this menu holds checkboxes, so it read focus on the first item as not moved.

Each checkbox keeps its name and state, and Enter lands focus on the first one with Tab stepping through the rest, so the filter is usable and the cost is a misleading menu announcement: low.

Esc closes the Upload bill popover and focus drops to the page body instead of returning to the Upload bill button, whether the popover was opened by click or by Enter on the focused button, so 2.4.3 fails. A keyboard user has to tab again from the top of the page, which is friction, so it stays low.

The avatar-only account menu button still has no accessible name on both sampled states: the probes read button "" [expanded=false, haspopup=menu], with no aria-label, title or text. It is the only entry to Profile, Notifications, Security and Log out, and keyboard users can Tab to it and open it with Enter, so the task is possible but the control cannot be identified. That is 4.1.2, and it stays medium: the button is not a form control or the page's sole primary action.

The chevron button that scrolls the timeline left has no accessible name on both sampled states: the probes read button "", the SVG is aria-hidden and the visually hidden label span is empty. It is fully transparent until hover, but Tab still reaches it, so a screen-reader user lands on an unnamed button. That is 4.1.2; it is a secondary pan control, not a primary action, so it stays medium.

The unnamed button is the disabled chevron-up carousel control in a stacked action row that is invisible (opacity 0, data-visible=false, pointer-events none) behind the visible Cancel and Save row, on both states. It still reaches the accessibility tree as button "" [disabled], so 4.1.2 fails, but sighted users never see it, nobody can activate it, and it is neither a form control nor the primary action, so it is low.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 passes: every result is selectable from the keyboard with ArrowDown and Enter while focus stays in the combobox, which is what the ARIA combobox pattern prescribes, so the listbox does not need to be a tab stop. 2.4.3 passes: Tab order runs search field, filter buttons, search field. 4.1.2 is a separate issue about the options' roles, covered by the aria-required-children finding.

value.name: Payments to review Uncategorized transactions
value.template: combobox "Payments to review Uncategorized transactions" [expanded=true, haspopup=listbox]

reason: The Tab walk reproduces: Tab cycles the search field and the filter buttons and never lands on the listbox. That is the combobox pattern, not a keyboard gap: focus stays in the search field, ArrowDown moves aria-activedescendant to the next result (the highlight moved to Review Jupiter Checking 4455 transactions), and Enter ran that result and set the query to Jupiter Checking 4455.

The listbox's only child is a ul. Chrome exposes it as listbox > list > listitem [level=1], and the li elements marked role=option appear as listitem with no option role, so screen readers do not announce the results as options (no selected state, no position in the set) while aria-activedescendant moves across them. Keyboard use still works, so the search is possible but harder to follow: medium.

The focus probe of the Search keyboard shortcuts field reproduces the sweep: focus changes 0 pixels around it (visible: false), and the computed outline is none. The field is the dialog's first stop, so a keyboard user sees only a caret. It sits in a help dialog, not a primary path, so it stays medium.

On the Assign Team Lunch step, Tab reaches Next on the fourth stop, and both Enter and Space activate it: the dialog moves to the Set up budget cards step (the sampled state). Keyboard users can operate the trigger, so 2.1.1 does not fail; focus does drop to body after activation, but Back and Assign are reachable by Tab, and that is a different problem from the one reported.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the WCAG input-purposes list (name, email, address, card number and so on). This field selects a card to link to a budget, so it has no such purpose and the invalid token takes nothing from users: nothing is left to identify. 4.1.2 is met: the accessibility tree gives the combobox its role, name Abigail Kyte and states (expanded=false, haspopup=listbox); an invalid autocomplete token changes none of them. 4.1.1 Parsing was removed in WCAG 2.2. No other A or AA criterion covers the attribute.
reason: The combobox carries autocomplete="garbage" next to the data-1p-ignore, data-lpignore and data-bwignore attributes, a deliberate switch-off of browser autofill. The field picks which card a team member's budget spend comes from; it does not collect information about the user and serves none of the 1.3.5 input purposes. It exposes role combobox, its name and its expanded state to the accessibility tree.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and whose purpose matches its list of input purposes (name, email, address and so on). This field is a budget form value (budget name, spend limit amount, description or spend-control mode), so no listed purpose applies and the invalid token blocks no autofill the user needs. 4.1.2 is unaffected: the accessibility tree still exposes the field's role, name and state (see the ax probes). 1.3.1 and 3.3.2 are met because the visible label is programmatically associated. The invalid token is an HTML conformance error, and 4.1.1 Parsing no longer exists in WCAG 2.2.

The Description textarea carries aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at an existing span, and Chrome exposes both (invalid=true, errormessage=Please complete this field), so its state and value are programmatically determinable. What is missing is redundancy: the span is not in a live region or aria-describedby, so a screen reader with weak aria-errormessage support may not read it on focus. aria-errormessage is optional ARIA and the submit-time announcement gap is the 4.1.3 finding, so the 4.1.2 impact is minor.

value.template: textbox "<amount>" [invalid=true, errormessage=Must be a dollar value.]

reason: The bill amount input, shown with the error Must be a dollar value., has no label element, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so its name is the 0.00 placeholder and the only text beside it is a $ prefix. Screen-reader users hear 0.00 instead of what the field is, which fails 3.3.2 and 4.1.2; the $ prefix and the error exposed through aria-errormessage keep the task possible, so it stays medium.

The bill amount input, holding 220.00, exposes as textbox named 0.00: it has no label element, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so the placeholder is its only name and the field's purpose is not announced (3.3.2, 4.1.2). The $ prefix and the value keep the task possible, so it stays medium.

The Invoice no. input (value INV-902) exposes as textbox with an empty name on both states: no label element, aria-label, labelledby or placeholder, and its visible label sits on the wrapping button instead. Shift+Tab from the input lands on that button, which says Invoice no., so users can tell what the field is, but the unnamed form control still fails 4.1.2 and 3.3.2: medium.

The Missing due date chip is a button with role menuitem, aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded=false inside a div with role menubar, so it is not a menuitem outside a menu or menubar as flagged. The menubar also holds Remove filter and Reset buttons and ignores arrow keys, but Tab reaches each control and Enter opens the chip's menu, so no A or AA criterion fails here.

The icon-only X (decline) button in the bulk-selection bar has no name on both states, and focusing it shows no tooltip or description, so a screen reader announces only "button". That fails 4.1.2. The bar's Review Requests button is named and leads to the same decisions, so the task stays possible and the finding stays medium.

The icon-only check (approve) button in the bulk-selection bar has no name on both states, and focusing it shows no tooltip or description, so a screen reader announces only "button" next to the unnamed decline button. That fails 4.1.2. The bar's Review Requests button is named and leads to the same decisions, so the task stays possible and the finding stays medium.

The Item 2 amount field's only accessible name is its placeholder, 0.00 (the Item 1 field has the same name), and the visible Unit price text above it is a plain span, not a label, so a screen reader announces 0.00 with no purpose and 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 fail (3.3.2 is met visually). Line Item and GL Code are named, so a user can work out the field by elimination: the task is hard but possible, medium.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 asks that all functionality work from a keyboard. Uploading a file does: Upload attachment on invoicing.edit-series (Enter and Space each click the overlay input) and Upload bill on billpay.inbox-after-payment (its popover input takes Tab focus). The overlay itself is inert for pointer users too (pointer-events none), so no function is mouse-only. 4.1.2 and 2.4.3 do not apply to an element that is not a control for any user. No other A or AA criterion covers it.
reason: The Choose Files input is an invisible overlay on a drop zone (opacity 0.00001, pointer-events none, tabindex -1), so a mouse click cannot reach it either. Keyboard users upload through the Upload attachment button, which takes Tab and clicks the same input on Enter and Space, and on Bill Pay through the Upload bill popover, whose own Choose Files input takes focus.

Tab walks of 94 and 98 stops on both states never land on the Status column header. It is a th with no tabindex, button or aria-sort, and the header sorts on mouse click (clicking Amount re-sorted the table on both states; Status is the same component with a click handler). Keyboard users cannot sort but every row stays readable, so the task is possible but harder.

On both states Tab never reaches the Amount column header, a th with no tabindex, button or aria-sort. A mouse click on it re-sorts the rows (220, 1,290, 11,600 became 11,600, 1,290, 220 on Bill Pay; the Payments approvals list reordered as well). Keyboard users cannot sort, but every row stays readable, so the task is possible but harder.

On both states Tab never reaches the Last updated column header, a th with no tabindex, button or aria-sort; the sort chevron shows it is a sortable column and the header carries a click handler. Keyboard users cannot sort, but every row stays readable, so the task is possible but harder.

The element is the Needs Approval tab: a plain div with no role, no tabindex and a click handler. Tab walks on both states skip it (on Payments only the selected Inbox tab takes focus). It is the only in-page way to the Needs Approval, Scheduled and Paid lists: the matching /bill-pay/approvals and /bill-pay/scheduled links sit in a display:none card and Payments has none. A keyboard user cannot open those lists from the page (AE7).

The row's trash button, a destructive hover action, exposes role button with an empty name on both states: no aria-label, no title, only an aria-hidden trash icon. It takes Tab focus, so keyboard and screen-reader users reach an unlabeled delete control. The labeled Delete in the detail panel sits inside an aria-hidden panel, so it is no equivalent for them. Medium: it is not a form control or the page's sole primary action.

The gear icon button beside the bill-forwarding email chip has no name on both states: no aria-label, title or text, and an aria-hidden svg. On Bill Pay it opens the Bill Pay settings modal and is the only control on the page that does. It fails 4.1.2. Medium: a secondary action, not the page's primary one.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.2 needs a name and role that software can read. The probes show role button and name Choose Files on both states, supplied by the browser's file input. The input is an invisible overlay that sits next to a visible, named Upload attachment button on invoicing and behind the named Upload bill popover on Bill Pay, so no user depends on its name. 3.3.2 and 2.4.6 are met by the visible labels of those controls. No other A or AA criterion fails.
reason: axe's label rule fires on the invisible drop-zone overlay input (opacity 0.00001, pointer-events none, tabindex -1), but the browser still names it Choose Files with role button, and nobody can see, click or tab to it. The usable controls, Upload attachment on invoicing and the Upload bill popover on Bill Pay, are named.

The detail-panel aside has aria-hidden=true, opacity 0 and a 200px offset, yet holds 12 tab stops (Close, amount, Review, Delete, date and invoice buttons, note, upload). On Bill Pay, Tab from the last row's Review reaches Delete inside it after four presses with nothing visible and the page shifts sideways; on Payments the walk also lands 12 stops in it. Fails 4.1.2 (focus inside aria-hidden content) and 2.4.7 (no visible focus). Medium: keyboard users can still finish, but lose focus for a dozen stops, one of them Delete.

All three parts reproduce. On both states the row's trash button is a role button with an empty name (no aria-label or title, aria-hidden svg); the Inbox, Needs Approval, Scheduled and Paid tabs are generic divs with no role or tabindex; and the amount input in the detail panel is a textbox named only by its placeholder, 0.00. Medium: nothing is blocked outright, and the amount input still reads as 0.00.

The row-number text measures 2.68:1 (#9d9da8 on #ffffff, 10px) on books.to-review where AA needs 4.5:1, so 1.4.3 fails. On books.bills the sweep's row no longer exists (the grid now holds 8 rows), so only to-review was measured. The numbers only index the rows and no task depends on them, so the impact is friction: low.

Tab onto the row-open button draws no indicator on books.bills and books.general-ledger (diff 0 against a floor of 16). The button has a 3px box-shadow ring, but the cell clips it, so the screenshots show nothing. The unnamed wrapper stop just before the button in the same cell does draw a ring, which keeps a keyboard user oriented, so it stays medium.

The row-number cell has a pointer cursor from its hover layer but no click behaviour. Clicking it on books.vendors (row 3, the sweep's element) and on the row 8 cell at the same coordinates on books.bills changes nothing: no selection, no dialog, no navigation, same URL. There is no click-only control to reach by keyboard.

Tab does reach this button. On books.bills the button at the sweep's position (1386,495, row 8) is stop 57 of 59 and a focus probe reaches it via tab. On books.reconciliation the button at the sweep's position (1386,1256, row 23) is reached via tab too, and a 170-press walk visits the button of every row up to 46. The grid reuses row nodes, so the sweep's xpaths (div[21], div[36]) no longer match the node at that position.
Reached books.bills twice and the xpath matched nothing both times. The live grid has 8 rows and no utility row, where the sweep's element sat in an animating utility row at y=567. Not retested.

The sort button in a column header has role button and an empty name on books.bills and in the books.coa-preview dialog, so 4.1.2 fails. Clicking the header text does not sort, so this button is the only way to sort and a screen-reader user hears just button. Sorting is secondary, so the task is possible but unclear: medium.

The row-open chevron button has role button and an empty name on books.to-review (row 15, the sweep's element) and on books.bills (row 8 at the sweep's position), so 4.1.2 fails. It is the only control that opens a row's detail: clicking row cells on both screens does not, and the button opens the bill drawer. A screen-reader user hears button for every row with nothing to say what it opens or which row it belongs to. The guidance rates the sole primary action high.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 needs a focus order that preserves meaning and operability: the sidebar menu comes first and the page it controls comes second, which matches the visual and DOM order of the two regions. 1.3.2 is met for the same reason, since the sequence of the sidebar and the main content is meaningful. The jump up the screen is the move from the end of one region to the start of the next, so neither criterion fails.
reason: Tab goes from Settings, the last link in the left sidebar, to the Pending close icon beside the period date under the page title, which is the first control of the page content. Navigation first and page content second is the layout's own reading order, and no control is skipped.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 needs an order that preserves meaning: each column is read top to bottom, then the next column to its right, and Tab does exactly that. 1.3.2 is met because the DOM sequence of the three sections matches their left-to-right visual sequence. A move from the bottom of one column to the top of the next fails neither criterion.
reason: The Books home page has three columns (Cash, Expenses, Revenue). Tab finishes the Expenses list at Computers and Hardware, then moves to the header of the Revenue column, View revenue at the top right. That is column-by-column reading order, so the upward jump is not out of order.

Ops / Payroll and Venus Credit Card are consecutive rows of the account list. With the page content scrolled to the top, Ops / Payroll sits at y 1489 and Venus at y 1534, 45px lower, so the order is forward. The sweep read Venus higher only because the content area scrolled from 634 to 780 when focus arrived.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 needs a focus order that preserves meaning and operability: the popover content comes right after its trigger and focus then continues to the next control, which is the order a keyboard user expects. 1.3.2 is met because the sequence follows the trigger-then-content relationship. The sweep's backward jump is only the popover sitting lower on screen than the top bar, so neither criterion fails.
reason: On books.home and books.accounts alike, focus on the Keyboard shortcuts button opens a popover below it. Tab goes trigger, then the popover's See all shortcuts link, then the next top-bar control to the right of the trigger, an account menu button. That is the normal order for a popover that follows its trigger, and no control is skipped. The account menu button has no name, which is a separate finding.

Benefits Expense and Payroll Taxes are consecutive rows of the Expenses list. With the page content scrolled to the top, Benefits sits at y 1305 and Payroll Taxes at y 1363, 58px lower, so the order is forward. The sweep read Payroll Taxes higher only because the content area scrolled from 463 to 780 when focus arrived.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 needs an order that preserves meaning: the Cash column is read top to bottom, then the Expenses column to its right, and Tab does exactly that. 1.3.2 is met because the DOM sequence of the sections matches their left-to-right visual sequence. A move from the bottom of one column to the top of the next fails neither criterion.
reason: Tab finishes the Cash column's account list at Petty Cash, then moves to the header of the Expenses column, View expenses at the top of the middle column. That is column-by-column reading order, so the upward jump is not out of order.

The Cash in vs out chart ends at y 948 with the page content scrolled to the top, and the By ledger account list starts below it at y 1129 with Jupiter Checking as its first row. The order chart, then list is forward. The sweep read Jupiter higher only because the content area scrolled from 67 to 602 when focus arrived.

Legal and Salaries and Wages are consecutive rows of the Expenses list. With the page content scrolled to the top, Legal sits at y 899 and Salaries at y 957, 58px lower, so the order is forward. The sweep read Salaries higher only because the content area scrolled from 57 to 436 when focus arrived.

The probe reproduces the sweep: Tab reaches the timeline's scroll-left button and it measures invisible. The button is at opacity 0 even while focused, so its focus ring is invisible too, and it has no name. It still works (Enter scrolled the timeline left by 115px, then Space by another 115px), so a sighted keyboard user operates a control they cannot see. criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 needs all functionality to work from a keyboard. Opening a month's report details is available from the keyboard: each month's bar is a focusable button labelled with its figures and 'Press Enter or Space to view report details', and Enter opens the same panel the overlay click opens. The overlay only carries the pointer hover and click, so no keyboard function is missing. 2.4.7 and 4.1.2 are not at issue for an element that carries no keyboard function of its own.
reason: The rect is a transparent overlay (fill transparent) over the plot area of the Cash in vs out chart, and a click on it opens the side panel for the month under the pointer. The four monthly bars in the same chart are buttons with tabindex 0 that the Tab walk reaches, and Enter on the August bar opened the same panel, so a keyboard user can do everything the click does.

Tab never reaches the marker cell for row 10: the walk goes from the Select all rows checkbox through the column headers to each row's chevron button, and the focus probe ends on body. The per-row Select row 10 checkbox inside the cell is display:none until the pointer hovers it, and focusing the row's chevron does not reveal it. Keyboard users can select every row or edit one transaction through its detail drawer, but cannot pick a few rows for the bulk bar (date, description, ledger account), so the task is possible but hard: medium.

Tab never reaches the marker cell for row 1: the walk goes from the Select all rows checkbox through the column headers to each row's chevron button, and the focus probe ends on body. The per-row Select row 1 checkbox inside the cell is display:none until the pointer hovers it, and focusing the row's chevron does not reveal it. Keyboard users can select every row or edit one transaction through its detail drawer, but cannot pick a few rows for the bulk bar (date, description, ledger account), so the task is possible but hard: medium.

The gear icon button at the top right of the account header is exposed as button "" with no name, so 4.1.2 fails. It is visible and focusable, and it opens the Account settings dialog (rename, opening balance, Delete account), so screen-reader users cannot tell what it does before they activate it. It is not a form control or the page's primary action, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the WCAG input-purpose list (name, email, address, card number and so on). The Reconciliation years combobox chooses which year of reconciliations to list, so it has no listed purpose and 1.3.5 cannot fail. 4.1.2 is met because the field exposes role combobox, name Reconciliation years and the expanded and haspopup states (see the ax probe). 4.1.1 Parsing no longer exists in WCAG 2.2, so an invalid token is only an HTML conformance error.
reason: The Reconciliation years combobox has autocomplete="garbage", a deliberate autofill opt-out. It picks which year of statements to show, not information about the user, so no listed input purpose applies, and the tree still exposes combobox "Reconciliation years" with its states.

The focus probe of the Tag name field reproduces the sweep: hidden is invisible, because the Create tag card (_creationCard) measures opacity 0 under the sweep's motion-off stylesheet. Kept under rule 1, as no probe passes. Check the harness: the card's own CSS is animation _fadeIn 0.3s forwards, and the sweep's injected animation: none !important removes it, so the card never reaches opacity 1; with that sheet cleared the card shows at opacity 1 (shot:a11y/runs/2026-10-03-1525/shots/verify/verify-112/books.tag-create-natural-motion.png), so real users likely see the field.

value.name: Tag name
value.template: textbox "Tag name" [invalid=true, errormessage=Tag name cannot be empty]

reason: Reproduced: the Tag name field has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at the error span, but that span has no role or aria-live and nothing in aria-describedby points to it. Chrome still exposes the field as invalid=true with errormessage=Tag name cannot be empty, so a screen reader that supports aria-errormessage reads the message on focus. The gap is the missing fallback for readers that do not, which weakens 4.1.2 a little; the announcement at submit is the separate status-message finding.

value.name: Tag name
value.template: textbox "Tag name" [invalid=true, errormessage=Tag name cannot be empty]

reason: After Save on an empty form, Tag name cannot be empty appears under the field while focus stays on the Save button. The text sits in a plain div with no role, no aria-live and no live-region ancestor, and aria-describedby does not point to it; the page's only role=alert node is empty. A screen reader user hears nothing and does not learn that the save failed, so 4.1.3 fails. It is a tag name, not a money movement, and the field is reachable and marked invalid, so it stays medium.

The 20x20 sort button next to the Date column header measures a 65 px clear circle on two successful reaches, well over the 24 px the spacing exception in 2.5.8 needs. The sweep read an offset of 0 for the same element; axe also passes it.

The Open combobox menu button has tabindex=-1 on both sampled states, so Tab skips it, as the sweep found. The same list opens from the keyboard: Tab reaches the combobox input (Select team members, Payment method) and ArrowDown expands it and a second ArrowDown selects an option. An equivalent keyboard path exists and the button is a redundant chevron, so only a minor 4.1.2/2.1.1 friction is left.

The trigger lives on cards.team-spend, the parent of the sampled state. Tab reaches the Assign budget to employees button in the Team Lunch row (the sweep's trace stopped on the table row that holds the button and pressed Enter and Space there), and on the button itself both Enter and Space open the Assign Team Lunch dialog and move focus into it.

The flagged listbox is an empty, 0x0 fixed-position live region (aria-live polite, no children, no options, empty aria-owns) that announces selected members; there is nothing in it to operate. The control that does the work, the Search by name or email combobox, is the first Tab stop in the dialog, followed by Import a CSV list, Cancel and Assign.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 needs a focus order that preserves meaning and operability. The page reads as a table on the left and a summary column on the right, and Tab follows that sequence, so meaning and operability hold. 1.3.2 needs a meaningful DOM sequence, and the DOM order matches the visual column order. The upward jump is a side effect of the two-column layout, not a reordering. The 13 hidden panel stops between the two are a separate focus-visible failure, not a focus-order one.
reason: Reproduced: after Sally Park, the last row of the Team member table, Tab goes to the info icon at the top of the right-hand Total budget column. That is the left column followed by the right column, which keeps the reading order, and the icon shows a visible focus ring and tooltip.

Tab reaches the tooltip anchor inside the closed Budget detail panel, which sits at opacity 0, shifted 200px right and marked aria-hidden. The focus probe finds it invisible, so a keyboard user loses focus on a stop that does nothing. It is one of 13 invisible stops, and the page stays usable past them, so it stays medium.

Tab lands on Remove From Budget inside the closed second panel (opacity 0, aria-hidden), and the focus probe finds it invisible. A keyboard user can fire a destructive action they cannot see, but the page's visible controls stay reachable, so it stays medium.

Tab lands on Customize inside the closed panel (opacity 0, aria-hidden). The focus probe finds it invisible, and the screenshot with focus on it shows no indicator anywhere on screen. The rest of the page stays reachable, so it stays medium.

The first Recent activity row in the closed panel takes Tab focus (tabindex 0) while the panel is at opacity 0, and the focus probe finds it invisible. Five activity rows are invisible stops. The rest of the page stays reachable, so it stays medium.

Edit in the closed Budget detail panel is a focusable span (role button, tabindex 0) at opacity 0, and the focus probe finds it invisible. On payments.taxes the Edit Filing action sits in a wrapper at opacity 0 that stays hidden on focus, and the probe finds it invisible too (the row gets a ring, but the action does not appear). Both states fail 2.4.7 with the same impact, so it stays medium.

The closed second panel is aria-hidden=true and holds three focusable controls (Close detail panel, a tabindex 0 tooltip anchor, Remove From Budget) that Tab reaches, so a screen-reader user lands on controls the tree hides. This fails 4.1.2. The ax probe shows the panel ignored. It hides one closed panel, not the page, and the page stays usable, so it stays medium.

On both sampled states the Name field has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing to a plain span with no live region or alert role, and its aria-describedby lists only the help text. The error appears after Save changes is pressed while focus stays on that button, so nothing announces it; a screen-reader user finds it only by going back to the field. The task is possible but hard, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 Status Messages covers messages that report the result of an action, a warning, an error or progress. The Budget name heading carries the placeholder class text-placeholder and only shows the preview card's title when the Name field is empty, so it is not a status message and 4.1.3 does not apply. 1.3.1 is met: the heading is a real h2 in the preview. The validation error itself is a separate span associated with the Name field, assessed in the aria-valid-attr-value finding.
reason: The reported text is the h2 of the preview card, which falls back to the placeholder Budget name while the Name field is empty. It mirrors the field and is not a status message; the actual error, Please complete this field, is a different element and is covered by the aria-errormessage finding.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order asks that focus move in an order that preserves meaning and operability. After Esc, focus returns to the menu button that started the interaction, the pattern the ARIA Authoring Practices set for a menu button whose item opens a dialog. The menuitem the sweep expected cannot take focus because the menu closes when the item is chosen. 3.2.1 On Focus and 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap are not in play: nothing changes on focus and Esc leaves the dialog. The dialog having no accessible name is a separate 4.1.2 question and not part of this finding.
reason: Reproduced on cards.cancel-card-confirm: Esc closes the dialog and focus lands on the More button, which has aria-haspopup=true and aria-expanded=false. The Cancel card menuitem is not in the DOM while the dialog is open and the menu is hidden afterwards, so More, the control that opened the menu, is where focus belongs.

After Freeze card is confirmed, the Freeze button is replaced by Unfreeze and Frozen badges appear on the list row and the card art. No toast shows, the page's status region stays empty, and focus is left on the page body, so nothing announces that the card is frozen. The freeze completes, but a screen-reader user gets no confirmation. Freezing is not a money movement, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 Status Messages covers content that reports the success or result of an action, a waiting state, progress or an error. The masked card number button is the card's regular face and a control that reveals data (ax name Click to reveal); it reports nothing about the unfreeze. 4.1.2 is met: the button has a name and role. The real status change, the Frozen badge going away and the toggle returning to Freeze, is assessed in the Freeze finding.
reason: The flagged element is the card face's Click to reveal button, which holds the masked card number, expiry and CVC. It is ordinary card content and a control, not a message about the result of Unfreeze. The unannounced result is the Freeze button and Frozen badge change, which the Freeze finding in this batch covers.

After Unfreeze card, the Frozen badges disappear and the Unfreeze button reverts to Freeze. No toast shows, the page's status region stays empty, and focus is left on the page body, so nothing announces that the card is active again. The task completes, but a screen-reader user gets no confirmation. Unfreezing is not a money movement, so it stays medium.

Probes measure #9d9da8 text at 2.58:1 on the create-budget preview card's "$0 monthly per person" line (15px, needs 4.5:1) and 2.68:1 on the greyed amount in the pending Jack Black scheduled-payment row. criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose covers only fields that collect information about the user and serve one of the listed input purposes (name, email, address and so on); a Monthly/Weekly frequency selector serves none, so an invalid token on it fails nothing. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value is met: the ax probes show combobox "Repeats" [expanded=false, haspopup=listbox] on both states. 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions is met by the visible Repeats label. criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose covers fields that collect information about the user and serve a listed input purpose; a search box for finding teammates serves none, so an invalid token on it fails nothing. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value is met: the ax probe shows textbox "Search team members". 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions is met by the accessible name and the Search for a name placeholder. It searches the team list for other people by name, so it does not collect the user's own information and 1.3.5 does not apply. The accessibility tree exposes it as textbox "Search team members".

The flagged element is the Employee budgets table, which is page content that loads after the redirect, not a status message. The real confirmation, the Budget published toast, is injected into #toast-container, a role=alert (assertive) region that is on the page and empty before the toast appears, and the table itself carries aria-live=polite.

The pending bar meter has no accessible name on both sampled states (probe shows meter ""), so it still fails 4.1.2. The card header shows the same figures as text: Spent this month $1,500.00 and $3.5k available · $5k spend limit, and the expanded details list Posted, Pending and Available to spend, so screen-reader users can still read the spend.

value.name: Spend limit
value.template: textbox "Spend limit" [invalid=true, errormessage=Must be a dollar value.]

Probe on cards.expense-decline measures the Decline label at 1.97:1 (#dfa2bf on #fdf7f9, 15px) against the 4.5:1 AA needs, and the guidance rates anything under 2:1 high. The button is only styled as disabled while Reason is empty: it exposes as an enabled button with no disabled state, stays focusable and still submits the form, so the inactive-component exception does not apply.

On both sampled states the Attachments label is a dt whose parent is a plain div, not a dl, so the tree exposes a term with no description list around it (1.3.1). It labels one section and the text still reads in order, so the impact is minor and it stays low.

The trash-can button beside demo-receipt.pdf in the expense panel exposes as button with an empty name: the icon is aria-hidden and there is no aria-label, title or tooltip, so screen-reader users get no cue that it deletes the attachment (4.1.2). Opening the file still works through the named neighbour and the button is not the primary action, so it stays medium.

The icon-only sort button beside the Status column header (and the other five on Bills, and those in the chart-of-accounts preview dialog) has an empty accessible name on both sampled states: the ax probes read button "" and the SVG is aria-hidden. Tab reaches it, there is no aria-label, title or tooltip, and Enter on the header cell does not sort, so it is the only way to sort and fails 4.1.2. Sorting is secondary to reading the table, so it is not the sole primary action and stays medium.

The chevron button at the end of each row has no name on both sampled states (ax probes read button ""; the SVG is aria-hidden and there is no label or tooltip), so it fails 4.1.2. It is the only focusable control that opens a bill or transaction: Enter on it opens the bill detail dialog, and the row itself is not focusable and holds no link. Keyboard and screen-reader users get eight identical unnamed buttons for the sole row action, which the guidance rates high. On Bills the sweep's xpath names row 21 where the live DOM has row 11 for the same element (rect [1386,495,29,34]), so that probe uses the live xpath.

The All tab in the Chart of Accounts and Transactions tab bars is a plain link inside a div styled as the selected tab (underline and darker text). It has no aria-current, so both ax probes read link "All" with states {} and a screen-reader user cannot tell which view is active, which fails 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 in a minor way. The links are named and work, and the page title and table show what is listed, so the impact is friction: low.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order asks that focus order preserve meaning and operability. Each row is walked left to right (amount, then its Copy button) and then the row below starts, which is how the table reads, and no control is skipped. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence holds for the same reason: the DOM order is the table's reading order. The 350 px rise the sweep measured comes from the grid scrolling back to the left on the wrap, not from focus moving up the table, so neither criterion fails.
reason: Tab does move from the last Copy button of one grid row to the first amount button of the row below, and the grid scrolls back to the left when it does. That is row-by-row order in a table, so the leftward jump is a line wrap, and the next row sits lower on both sampled states.

Tab reaches the first amount button of the row on both sampled states and the button is not clipped: two probes on the Balance Sheet read visible with a 1311 and 1304 pixel focus change, and the Cash Flow probe reads 922. A hand Tab from the previous row's Copy button also lands it fully inside the grid; the amount buttons that really are covered by the frozen Oct MTD column are the ones in the focus-not-visible finding.

The amount button measures no focus change (0 px) on both Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss. Walking one Balance Sheet row by Tab, the frozen Oct MTD column covers or pushes off screen the buttons in columns 7, 8 and 12 (the sweep's 21,208,174.05 sits at x 1393 in a 1440 px viewport), while the other seven keep their ring and the figures stay readable, so it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies to fields that collect information about the user and serve one of the purposes in its list, such as name, email or address. The value garbage is set on purpose, next to data-1p-ignore, data-lpignore and data-bwignore, to keep password managers and browsers from offering autofill, and it does not change the role, name or state the tree exposes, so 4.1.2 holds. No other A or AA criterion covers an autocomplete token.
reason: The frequency combobox carries autocomplete="garbage", a deliberate token that switches browser autofill off, on a Monthly/year report filter that collects nothing about the user. The accessibility tree still exposes combobox "frequency" on both sampled states.

reason: The years combobox carries autocomplete="garbage", a deliberate token that switches browser autofill off, on a Monthly/year report filter that collects nothing about the user. The accessibility tree still exposes combobox "years" on both sampled states.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus follows the rows in reading order, and the step from the last cell of Bill Pay Clearing to the first cell of Payroll Clearing is the expected next stop; the upward move on screen comes from the grid scrolling, not from the order. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence: the DOM runs row by row and left to right, which matches the visual layout. No other A or AA criterion covers where the next stop appears on screen.
reason: The jump reproduces at stop 519 on books.cash-flow: Tab moves from the Copy button in the last cell of the Bill Pay Clearing row to the first amount button of the next row, Payroll Clearing, which lands 350px higher on screen. The grid's own scroll container moved 386px (scrollTop 404 to 790) as focus entered the next row, so the order is still row by row, left to right.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus goes to the next row in sequence on both screens (row 29 to 30, row 24 to 25), so the order keeps its meaning; the upward move on screen is the grid's scroll. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence: the DOM follows the visual row order. No other A or AA criterion applies to where the next stop appears on screen.
reason: The jump reproduces at the sweep's stops on both states. On books.chart-of-accounts Tab moves from the row 29 button (y=865) to the row 30 wrapper (y=505); on books.reconciliation from row 24 (y=865) to row 25 (y=505). On books.coa-dropdown, Escape closes the Chart of accounts listbox and document.activeElement becomes body instead of the Default (Recommended) combobox that opened it; reproduced on two fresh reaches, with aria-expanded going to false. On both states Tab lands on the unnamed expand button in a second copy of the drawer's action row that sits at opacity 0 under the visible row (focus probes: visible false, hidden invisible). The visible Cancel and Save come first, so the task stays possible. In the sweep's motion-off environment the row never fades in, and I could not probe without it.

On both states Tab lands on the Save button in the same hidden copy of the action row (opacity 0, covered by the visible row), and the focus probes report visible false. The visible Save is reachable earlier in the walk, so the task stays possible. In the sweep's motion-off environment the row never fades in, and I could not probe without it.

Tab reaches the Date field at stop 19 from the drawer's first button, but the field is swapped for an editing input rendered in a portal at the end of the page and focus drops to body, so the walk never rests on Date. Tab then moves on to Description, and the portal input is reachable only after the whole drawer. The date is prefilled and the editor is reachable out of order, so the task is hard, not blocked.

A manual Tab walk from the drawer's first button reaches the select-all checkbox at stop 21, right after Description. The sweep's walk ended at stop 19, where focus drops to body at the Date field; that failure is the Date finding.

A manual Tab walk from the drawer's first button reaches the plus-icon button in the last line-item row at stop 29. The sweep's walk ended at stop 19, where focus drops to body at the Date field; that failure is the Date finding.

A manual Tab walk from the drawer's first button reaches the xmark-icon button in the second line-item row at stop 28. The sweep's walk ended at stop 19, where focus drops to body at the Date field; that failure is the Date finding.

The icon-only xmark button in the second line-item row exposes role button with an empty name (ax probe), so 4.1.2 fails and screen-reader users cannot tell what it does. The entry can still be saved, so medium.

Reproduced on the open listbox: the combobox value is Monthly, but the option exposed as selected is Annual (selected=true, while Monthly is selected=false). Reproduced: the Save button in the drawer header has opacity 0.4 and background rgb(82, 102, 235), but disabled is false, aria-disabled is absent and the tree exposes button "Save" with no disabled state. The wizard swaps its steps in place at the same URL with an unchanged title, and focus ends on body, so a screen-reader user who pressed Confirm hears nothing about the order or the deactivated old card. Not a money movement, so it stays medium.

The 0000 placeholder in the PIN field, and the two digits left over after typing 12, measure 1.41:1 (#d5d6db on #fbfcfd) on both states, where AA needs 3:1 for 38px text. It is real text, not decoration: it is the only visible cue that the PIN has four digits before the error appears. Under 2:1 is high by the guidance.

The save label measures 1.82:1 (#babbc0 on #f9f9fb, 13px) on both states against 4.5:1. The button only looks inactive: it has no disabled or aria-disabled, keeps the pointer cursor, and on the error state a click on it returned Must be 4 digits, so the inactive-component exception does not apply. The label reads at full contrast once a valid PIN is typed, but the guidance puts a sole action's label under 2:1 at high.

The only field on the Change PIN screen is exposed as textbox with no name: no label element, no aria-label, an empty placeholder. Enter a new PIN: is a plain span beside it and is not associated, so a screen-reader user tabbing into the field hears no prompt. An unnamed form control is high by the guidance.

On the too-short state the PIN field is still exposed as textbox with no name, no aria-invalid and no aria-describedby, so neither its purpose nor the Must be 4 digits error is tied to it. An unnamed form control is high by the guidance.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 covers messages that report success, results, progress or errors. These spans only echo what the user typed or pad the field with placeholder digits: they sit in the field's pointer-events:none mirror container, behind the input, and report no outcome. The field's own value is exposed by the input element. The one real error, Must be 4 digits, is a separate finding. No other A or AA criterion fails for this claim.
reason: The span holds the 00 placeholder digits that fill the PIN field after typing 12. It is part of the field's visual mirror, not a status message.

After save, Must be 4 digits appears in a plain span: it sits in no live region, the input has no aria-describedby or aria-invalid, the page's only alert region (toast-container) is empty and focus stays on the save button. A screen-reader user gets no sign that the PIN was not saved. Not a money movement, so it stays medium.
