The Adyen N.V. merchant name in the subscription row is a plain span inside a mouse-only row: Tab never reaches it (focus probe via null, end exit), so the finding is real. An equivalent keyboard path exists: Tab lands on the row's invisible arrow button (opacity 0, no outline, no name), and Enter on it opens the same Adyen N.V. detail panel. The task is possible but hard, because a keyboard user cannot see or identify that stop.

Tab order in the detail panel runs top to bottom: Jane B. card link, its tooltip anchor, then the Oct 3 charge link. The reported rise of 196px comes from the page scrolling 460px when focus moves to the charge link (viewport y 720 to 524). In content coordinates the position goes from 720 to 984, which is forward.

The link shows the text View more and has aria-label View other transactions, so the visible label is not in the name and 2.5.3 fails. Voice-control users who say View more will not activate it. It is a secondary link, the name still describes the destination for screen-reader users, and number overlays work as a fallback, so the impact is friction.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order needs focus to move in an order that preserves meaning and operability. After Escape, focus is on the user menu trigger (button, aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded=false), the same place a keyboard user lands after closing any menu, and the menu it came from is gone. Focus is not lost to body and the next Tab continues from the trigger. 2.4.7 passes, since the trigger shows a focus ring. APG would close only the submenu and return to the parent menuitem, but that is a best practice the criterion does not require. No other A or AA criterion covers it.
reason: Reached home.appearance-submenu and pressed Escape: the submenu and the whole user menu close together, and focus lands on the avatar button that opened the menu, with a visible ring. The Appearance menuitem no longer exists, so focus returned to the control that launched the menu rather than being lost.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard needs every function to work from the keyboard. The skipped button is the segment already showing, and activating it does nothing (Space left the view unchanged). Showing the table, the only function it ever has, is reachable by Tab then Enter from the graph view, and the view toggles both ways with focus kept on the pressed button. 2.4.3 holds because the order stays logical. 4.1.2 (whether a selected segment exposes its state) is a different claim from the one this finding makes and was not tested here. No A or AA criterion fails on keyboard reach.
reason: Reproduced: on home.balance-table the Balance table button is the selected segment and carries tabindex=-1, so Tab skips it. The only other segment, Balance graph, is in the tab order. Enter on it switches the view and the roles swap, so a keyboard user can reach both views, and Space on the already-selected button changed nothing.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve one of the 53 purposes in the Input Purposes list (name, email, street-address, and so on). Industry is a custom picklist with five options and maps to none of them, so the invalid autocomplete token fails nothing. 4.1.2 passes: the ax probe shows role combobox, name Industry, expanded and haspopup exposed. 4.1.1 Parsing no longer exists in WCAG 2.2. Every other form field in the dialog uses the valid token off.
reason: The Industry combobox does carry autocomplete="garbage", which is not a valid token. But Industry is a five-item picklist (Startup, Ecommerce, Crypto, Consulting, Investing) and is not one of the 53 input purposes that 1.3.5 lists, so no AA criterion fails. The name and role still reach the accessibility tree as combobox "Industry".

The This Month date-range chip is a button with role=menuitem and aria-haspopup=menu inside a role=menubar, but it opens a date-range picker (a preset combobox, From and To fields and a month grid), not a menu. The menubar also has no menu keyboard model: both items are separate tab stops and ArrowLeft and ArrowRight leave focus on This Month. Screen-reader users hear "menu item, has popup menu" and are led to expect arrow-key navigation and a menu of items, which fails 4.1.2; Tab and Enter still work, so the task is possible but misleading.

The avatar button at the top right of Books home has no accessible name on both sampled states: the ax probes read button "" [expanded=false, haspopup=menu], the image inside has alt="" and there is no aria-label or title. Enter opens the user menu (Profile, Notifications, Security, Privacy, Perks, Appearance, Log out), so this fails 4.1.2 for a control that leads to account settings. Screen-reader users still hear that it opens a menu and the menu items are named, so the task is possible but unclear: medium.

The chevron-left button on the Books home timeline has no accessible name on both sampled states (ax probes read button ""; the SVG is aria-hidden), so it fails 4.1.2. It sits at opacity 0 until the timeline is hovered and stays invisible when focused. It only scrolls the month axis, and the selected range cannot be moved by keyboard anyway (ArrowLeft and Enter on the range do nothing), so the missing name adds friction rather than blocking a task: low.

The X icon button at the end of the last line row in the Create journal entry grid has no accessible name: the ax probe returns button "", the SVG is aria-hidden and there is no aria-label or text. The expand icon button in the drawer header has no accessible name on both sampled states: its visually hidden label span is empty and the ax probe returns button "". The plus icon button in the footer row of the Create journal entry grid has no accessible name: the ax probe returns button "" and the SVG is aria-hidden. This fails 4.1.2, and a screen-reader user cannot tell it adds a line. It is not the sole primary action, so it stays medium.

It is disabled and sits in a carousel action row that is invisible (data-visible=false, opacity 0, pointer-events none), so nobody can operate it and a screen-reader user only meets a stray unavailable button. Minor impact.

The Status column's sort button on the empty Payroll grid has no accessible name (ax probe button "" [disabled=true]), so 4.1.2 still fails. The grid is a skeleton placeholder behind the Payroll account will show up here message and the button is disabled, so nobody can operate it. Minor impact.

The value is invalid HTML and most likely a way to stop browser autofill, but no A or AA criterion requires a valid token on such a field. 4.1.2 is unaffected: the ax probe shows role textbox with the name Receipt required if transaction amount exceeds. 3.3.2 is met by the visible label.

Enter on Mileage selects it, then Expense becomes the tab stop and takes focus on Shift+Tab, so no function is out of keyboard reach. No A or AA criterion fails.
reason: Tab goes from the Create Merchant Card link at the bottom of the promo card to its dismiss X in the top-right corner, 88px higher, with no scrolling. The upward move comes from the two cards' different layout, not from content read out of order. No other A or AA criterion covers it.
reason: Tab stop 46 does jump 88px up, from the last segment of the spend bar in the Budget spend summary card to View all in the Review required card beside it. That is the move from one side-by-side card to the next: both cards read left to right in DOM order, and the three Review required links (View all, 5 expenses, 1 receipt exception request) follow in sequence on both states.

The tabs are plain divs with no role, no name and no tabindex: focus() on one returns false, Enter and Space do nothing, and the ax probes show role generic with an empty name on all three sampled states. A search query for other team members has no listed purpose, so the invalid token fails nothing. 4.1.2 passes: the field exposes role textbox and the name Search team members. 3.3.2 passes: the field has a label and a placeholder.

Both probes came back incomplete, so I read the computed colors. On cards.team-spend the flagged letter is the aria-hidden B in a team avatar, #535461 on its #cfe6e3 circle, 5.73:1, which passes. criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus moves into the popover on open and the next Tab reaches its only control, so the order preserves meaning and operability. 2.1.1 Keyboard: the switch is reachable and toggles with the keyboard. 4.1.2: the switch exposes role switch and the name Include non-budget spend. Focusing the container before the first item is an APG preference, and the container has no menu items to start on, so no A or AA criterion fails here.
reason: Opening the display options popover puts focus on the popover itself, which is the sweep's reading, and the popover holds one control: the Include non-budget spend switch. One Tab lands on that switch, labelled and operable, so a keyboard user loses no control and no content.

The popover is role=menu but its only content is an input with role=switch, so it has no menuitem children and breaks the menu pattern, a 4.1.2 role mismatch. reason: The stop is the Add button in the Accounts card's header, reached after Last 30 days in the balance card on its left (page y 340 to 269). Focus moves from the end of the balance card to the start of the Accounts card, the next card in the row, on both sampled states.

A real Tab from the search field lands on the All chip for about 17 ms, then the dialog closes and focus returns to Search for anything, so the Cards chip and the other filters cannot be used from the keyboard (2.1.1, and 3.2.1 because focus closes the dialog). Tab to the Approvals chip changes 0 pixels on both states. The chip sits past the right edge of the chip row, clipped under the Scroll filters right arrow, so focus lands on something nobody can see. The next stop (Users) scrolls the row and shows focus, and the other chips draw a ring, so the harm is one invisible stop, not a lost task.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 asks that the function work from a keyboard, not that every element is a tab stop. The results are operable from the input with the arrow keys and Enter, which is the APG combobox pattern (probe: the combobox controls this listbox). 2.4.3 and 4.1.2 are not at issue for a popup kept out of the Tab order. reason: The listbox is the popup of a combobox, so it is deliberately not a tab stop. Focus stays in the input and ArrowDown or ArrowUp move aria-activedescendant through the options, as the screenshot shows; the footer lists Enter to open the page.

The listbox's only child is a ul (div role=listbox > ul > li), which ARIA does not allow, so 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 fail. Chrome exposes the role=option items as unnamed listitems inside a list, not as options, which weakens the results list for screen-reader users; arrow-key navigation still works, so the task stays possible but hard.

On both states the role=option items sit in a ul instead of directly in the listbox, and Chrome exposes each one as listitem with an empty name and no selected state (ax probes). A screen-reader user arrowing through results gets unnamed list items, which makes the search hard but not impossible.

The ul inside the listbox has role=option children on both states, and it is exposed as list with no name (ax probes), which breaks 1.3.1. It shares its root cause with the aria-required-parent finding, which carries the impact, so this one stays low.

Pages is a filter chip inside the already-open search dialog, not a trigger that opens one. Reproduced: with a query typed, Tab from the input closes the dialog and returns focus to Search for anything, so the chip is out of reach from the keyboard (2.1.1). An equivalent path exists: on the empty dialog Tab reaches Pages, Enter selects it, Shift+Tab twice returns to the input, and typing card keeps the filter (screenshots). Filtering after typing is the hard part, so lowered from high to medium.

On both states the link is regular-weight rgb(70,91,209) inside a sentence of rgb(83,84,97), with text-decoration none at rest (underline on hover only), so the pair is 1.3:1 where 1.4.1 needs 3:1 without another cue. The contrast probe passes at 5.71:1, but it measures the link against white, a different pair, so it does not answer this finding. The address stays readable and is named in the sentence, so a user who cannot see the link still gets the address; below the guidance's high, it stays medium.

value.name: Product Search
value.template: combobox "Product Search" [expanded=false, haspopup=listbox, invalid=true, errormessage=Please complete this field]

reason: Product Search has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at a span that exists and reads Please complete this field, and Chrome's tree exposes it. The span is not a live region and is not in aria-describedby, so AT that ignores aria-errormessage says only that the field is invalid, which weakens 4.1.2 a little. aria-errormessage is optional ARIA and the error text is visible, so the impact is minor.

The unit price input has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at a span that exists and reads Please complete this field, and Chrome's tree exposes it as errormessage. The span is not a live region and is not in aria-describedby, so AT with weak aria-errormessage support gets the invalid state without the text, which weakens 4.1.2 a little. aria-errormessage is optional ARIA and the error text is visible, so the impact is minor.

After Next with an empty line item, both Please complete this field messages appear visibly, but the page's role=status and role=alert regions stay empty and do not change on a second Next, the messages sit in plain spans, and focus stays on Next. A screen-reader user hears nothing, so 4.1.3 fails. It is form validation on invoice setup, not the only confirmation of a money movement, so it stays medium.

On Customers, the edit and invoice icon buttons in every row have no aria-label, title or text, and the tree exposes button with an empty name, so a screen-reader user hears two identical buttons per row; the Edit customer tooltip appears only on mouse hover. On Branding, the swatch radios do have names, but they are slugs such as white-theme, so the unnamed-control claim holds on the primary state only.

The first Customers row's edit button and the trash button in the Wire Drawdowns detail card each expose button with an empty name: no text, aria-label or title, and the icon is aria-hidden. On Wire Drawdowns the unnamed Delete sits next to an unnamed Edit, so a screen-reader user cannot tell them apart, but the task is still possible, so medium.

Tab order on Edit recurring series runs Payer memo, Upload attachment, Internal note, matching the page: the link sits below the memo box and above Internal set up. The 208 px rise came from the form scrolling 293 px when Upload attachment took focus, not from a backward jump.

Tab to the Close button (stop 21) draws a box-shadow ring, but the toolbar band covers the button, so no pixels change on screen (diff 0, visible false). The visible x in the toolbar at stop 4 shows focus, so the exit stays available and the impact is one invisible stop.

The visible x in the Editing Series Template toolbar is an icon-only button with no name (4.1.2). A named Close button elsewhere on the page does the same thing (both return to the series page), so the task stays possible; rated low.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the Input Purposes list. An invoice number prefix serves none, so the invalid token fails no requirement. 4.1.2 is met: the field exposes role textbox and the name Invoice prefix More info. No other A or AA criterion covers the autocomplete attribute.
reason: The Invoice prefix field carries autocomplete="garbage", a deliberate way to switch off browser autofill, on both states. The field holds a series prefix (S-0003, INV), not information about the user.

The Status filter is a role=menu div that holds a fieldset of native checkboxes, not menuitems, so it fails 1.3.1 and 4.1.2. Opening it puts focus on the menu div and ArrowDown moves nothing; keyboard users must Tab to the checkboxes, so the task is possible but the menu role promises arrow-key behavior it does not have.

The listbox popup has no aria-label or aria-labelledby and exposes as listbox "" on both the member picker and the NetSuite GL code dropdown, so it still fails 4.1.2. Focus stays on the combobox that owns it (aria-controls points at the popup), and on the member picker that combobox is named Select team members, so users still learn which field they are in. The missing popup name is friction.

The Icon picker button has aria-label bolt selected, which overrides its label element, so its accessible name leaves out the visible label Icon shown above it. That fails 2.5.3 on both states: speech-input users cannot say Icon to reach it, and screen-reader users hear the current value but not what the field is. The task stays possible, so the default medium stands.

The This budget starts trigger is named by its label alone, so the date on the button (Aug 19, 2026) is not exposed; the probes show name This budget starts and no value, which fails 4.1.2. The button is disabled, so nobody can operate it, and the same date is stated in the Active dates panel beside the form (Starts August 19, 2026). The impact is minor.

The This budget ends trigger is named by its label alone, so the chosen value (Never) is not exposed in its name or description; the probes show name This budget ends and no value. A screen-reader user editing the end date cannot tell what it is set to without leaving the control, which fails 4.1.2. The task is possible, so medium stands.

The Icon picker button has aria-label dollar sign selected, which overrides its label element, so its accessible name leaves out the visible label Icon shown above it. That fails 2.5.3 on both states: speech-input users cannot say Icon to reach it, and screen-reader users hear the current value but not what the field is. The task stays possible, so the default medium stands.

The This budget starts trigger is enabled and named by its label alone, so the chosen date (Oct 3, 2026) is not exposed in its name or description; the probes show name This budget starts and no value on both states. A screen-reader user cannot tell the start date without leaving the control, which fails 4.1.2. The task is possible, so medium stands.

The amount in the card panel header is a link whose only name is $1,500.00. It has no underline, title or aria text, and its container holds no heading, so neither the text nor its context says it opens this card's transactions for Oct 1 to 3. That narrowly fails 2.4.4. The same panel has a Transactions button that opens this card's transactions (checked: it goes to /transactions filtered to the card), so nobody is blocked.

The 40x40 trash button in the Temporary limit change scheduled card has no accessible name (probe: button ""). Its Cancel scheduled limit change tooltip shows on hover only, and no aria-describedby or aria-labelledby points at it, so a screen-reader user cannot tell the button cancels the scheduled change. That fails 4.1.2. It is not the modal's primary action, so medium stands.

The nickname field has no label element, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so its name comes from the placeholder and is announced as Jane’s Credit Card, an example nickname, not the field's purpose. The visible hint Something short but memorable is not linked (aria-describedby points at a helptext id that does not exist) and the dialog itself has no name. That fails 3.3.2 and 4.1.2. A name exists and the task is possible, so medium stands.

The trash button next to demo-receipt.pdf has no accessible name (probe: button ""). Its Delete file tooltip shows on hover only, and nothing links it to the button, so a screen-reader user cannot tell it removes the attachment. That fails 4.1.2. It is one of two controls on the attachment, not the sole primary action, so medium stands.

The X button that dismisses the Require receipts banner has no name: its only content is an aria-hidden icon, and the ax tree shows button "" on both sampled states, so it fails 4.1.2. Enter dismisses the banner, which is an optional recommendation the Cards page works without, so the impact is minor.

The Add filter button opens a filter popover but carries no aria-expanded or aria-haspopup on either sampled state, so its open state is not exposed (4.1.2). Enter moves focus to the first filter tab, so a user learns it opened, which keeps the impact minor; Escape then drops focus to the page body instead of the button.

The card display is one button whose aria-label "Click to reveal" replaces its visible text ("•••• •••• •••• 0330 Exp CVC"), so the name omits the visible words and digits and fails 2.5.3; screen-reader users also never hear the last four digits before the reveal. The name states the action, the same words show as a tooltip on focus, and after the reveal the fields become buttons named from their content ("Click to copy 4111 ..."), so the impact is minor.

Light mode is exposed as menuitem with no checked state, so its selected or unselected state is not in the accessibility tree. The three theme options are plain menuitems with no menuitemradio role and no aria-checked; the check icon beside the selected option is aria-hidden, so which theme is active is shown visually only (4.1.2, 1.3.1). The parent Appearance item reads System default in its name and the options still work, so the impact is minor.

No other A or AA criterion covers the list's name.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 asks for a focus order that preserves meaning and operability. Here Tab moves left to right across each row and top to bottom between rows, and focus lands visibly on each stop, so meaning and operation are intact. 1.3.2 (Meaningful Sequence) holds too: the DOM order matches the visual reading order. A small rise from one column's input to the next column's label is how a two-column row reads, so no A or AA criterion fails.
reason: The 36px rise is from the sparkle button inside the Invoice number field to the info icon in the PO number label, which sits above its own input. Tab visits Invoice number, its sparkle, the PO number info icon and input, then the Invoice date row, which is the order the row reads in.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 applies to fields that collect information about the user and map to one of the 53 input purposes (name, email, street address, card number and so on). Invoice date holds the date the invoice is issued, so the criterion does not apply, and an invalid token on it fails nothing. 4.1.2 is unaffected: the probe reports name "Invoice date" and role textbox. 4.1.1 no longer exists in WCAG 2.2.
reason: The Invoice date field carries autocomplete="garbage", a token that suppresses browser autofill. The field holds the date the invoice is issued, which is invoice data and not one of the user-information purposes that 1.3.5 covers, and the ax probe shows its name and role intact.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the tree exposes the element as generic with an empty states object, so no state or value is misreported through aria-readonly; the attribute is dropped by the browser. 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: the attribute carries no information or relationship that sighted users get and assistive technology misses. reason: On both sampled states the element is a react-virtualized list div with role=presentation, tabindex=0, aria-label="grid" and aria-readonly="true". The accessibility tree exposes it as a generic named grid with no states, so the browser ignores aria-readonly and assistive technology is told nothing wrong by it. The attribute is invalid but has no effect on what users get, and the user-facing problem is the grid label, which is covered by the aria-prohibited-attr finding.

The list div carries aria-label="grid" on a role=presentation element, and the accessibility tree exposes it as a generic named grid. It is also a tabindex=0 stop: on payments.send-multiple-gl, Tab goes from the Break line items by Amount button to this empty zero-height div, announced as grid, and then on to Add line item. No grid exists, so the name misdescribes the element and 4.1.2 fails, but the user can Tab on and no control is blocked, so it is friction.

Reproduced on both sampled states: Escape from the open recipient menu does not return focus to its trigger button but leaves the Send flow. It lands on the Search combobox of the payment start page on payments.send-recipient-more-menu, and on the Close detail panel button of the Bill Pay inbox on billpay.recipient-card-menu. On the Bill Pay state, Escape also discards the recipient details already filled in (Debug LLC and its address). A keyboard or screen-reader user who presses Esc to close the menu loses the payment in progress, so the task is possible but hard, and 2.4.3 fails.

The file-upload handle at the right edge of the Send flow is a visible, focusable icon-only button that the tree exposes as button with an empty name, on both sampled states. Enter on it opens the attachment drop zone, whose only file input is out of the Tab order, so no labelled control stands in for it. Attaching a file is optional, so the payment itself is not blocked and it stays medium.

The ellipsis button on the recipient card has an empty name and announces only as a menu button, on both sampled states. Enter opens a menu holding Edit recipient details and Pay different recipient, so a screen-reader user cannot tell what the button offers. Go back and the bank-details Edit button cover part of it, so the task is possible but hard: medium.

reason: The Start on field is the payment's start date, and it carries autocomplete="garbage" on both sampled states. The page uses a junk token to switch autofill off for fields that are not one of the listed input purposes, and the field is a payment date, not information about the user.

The Number of payments before ending field measures 20 by 24 px with a 0 px clear circle on both sampled states, where 2.5.8 needs 24 by 24 or 24 px of spacing. The group is disabled on the sampled states (axe skips it, which is why it disagreed), but choosing a repeat frequency and the After radio enables the field at the same 20 by 24 px with offset 0, so the failure is live. It is a two-digit count box with a visible label, so the impact is friction: low.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order needs an order that preserves meaning and operability. Every control on Send: how to start receives focus, in reading order from the upload zone to the recipient list, and the Close button comes last as the way out; no required control is skipped or reachable only out of sequence. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence holds for the same reason. 2.1.1 holds because Close is Tab-reachable (probe-4801a5160634 shows via tab) and Escape also closes the flow, and 2.4.7 holds because the probe measured a visible focus ring (visible true, 332 px changed). A visual position away from the DOM position is a best practice, not an A or AA failure.
reason: Real Tab presses reproduce the jump: Search, Create recipient, Invite recipient, the three recipients, then Close at the top right as stop 12, with the map button after it. Close sits last in the DOM like a dismiss control after the content, every control is reached in a logical order, and Escape closes the flow with focus on the page body.

The drop zone's file input exposes the browser's own name, button "Choose File", with no author label, while the zone's visible text reads Drag and drop here or click to upload. The control is named, focusable and sits under the Upload a bill heading, so a screen-reader user can still attach a bill; the generic name that does not match the visible text is a minor 4.1.2 and 2.5.3 gap, not an unnamed control.

The Search combobox reports expanded=true and aria-controls="downshift-0-menu", but no element on the page has that id and the only listbox (id :re:) is hidden with display none, so a screen reader announces an open combobox with no list. The recipients below are ordinary buttons in the Tab order, so the task is unaffected, which makes it minor impact on 4.1.2: low.

Tab from the Missing label in the Ava Johnson row goes to that row's Remove and Edit buttons, then to the Noah Miller row directly below it, so focus follows the visual order. The table's scroll container moves 463px to bring the row into view, which is why the sweep read a y of 865 and then 452.

Tab reaches the Bob_Padilla_W-9.pdf button, but it sits in the closed Filing detail panel (aria-hidden, opacity 0, shifted 200px right), so nothing on screen shows where focus is; the probe reports it invisible. It is one of eight consecutive invisible stops in that panel, and no task is blocked, so it stays medium.

Tab reaches the Remove Bob_Padilla_W-9.pdf button inside the closed Filing detail panel (aria-hidden, opacity 0), and the probe reports it invisible. A keyboard user who presses Enter here acts on a control they cannot see; no task is blocked, so it stays medium.

Tab reaches the View Payments button inside the closed Filing detail panel (aria-hidden, opacity 0), and the probe reports it invisible; focusing it moves the page and shows no ring. One of eight consecutive invisible stops in that panel, no task blocked, so it stays medium.

Tab never lands on the 1099-MISC column header: the th has no tabindex and no button inside, and the probe finds no Tab stop for it. A click on it sorts the table. The first row becomes Mason Taylor after a click. Keyboard users cannot sort, but every row stays reachable, so it stays medium.

Tab never lands on the Name column header: the th has no tabindex and no button inside, and the probe finds no Tab stop for it. A click on it sorts the table. The rows run A to Z after a click. Keyboard users cannot sort, but every row stays reachable, so it stays medium.

The 1099 Filing and Tax Documents tabs are plain divs with no role or tabindex; Tab goes from Add to bookmarks straight past them on both states, and a click on either one switches page. The bar appears as soon as a row is selected and the invisible stop is a single one at the end of the page, so the failure of 2.4.7 has minor impact: low.

The Done button is keyboard-operable. The sweep stopped on the button's tooltip wrapper div (tabindex 0), where Enter and Space do nothing; one more Tab reaches the inner Done button, and Enter on it opens the 1099 payee panel and moves focus to Close detail panel. The extra wrapper tab stop is a separate nuisance, not an unreachable trigger.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: the sequence is toggle, then plan columns left to right, then the dialog's close button; it preserves meaning and operability, and a close control placed last in a dialog is a common pattern, so the visual jump costs no one a function. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence: the DOM reading order (title, billing toggle, plans, close) is coherent. reason: The close button is the last focusable element inside the dialog, so Tab reaches it after the plan buttons even though the X is drawn at the top right. Focus stays inside the dialog, every control is reachable in a meaningful order, and Escape also closes it.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: the plans are laid out in three columns and focus visits them column by column, each column's own controls together, which preserves meaning and operability; no control is skipped and none is out of reach. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence: DOM order matches the visual column order. A backward move on screen between columns is not by itself a failure of either criterion.
reason: Tab goes from Explore Pricing, the link at the foot of the Mercury column, to Select at the top of the Mercury Plus column. That is column-by-column order, the way the plans are read, so the upward jump follows the layout.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard: the only action Pay monthly performs is selecting monthly billing, which is already selected, so nothing is lost by skipping it; the other option is focusable and switches the view, and the walk in the annual state reaches Pay monthly on the first Tab, so every function stays operable. No other A or AA criterion fails on its tab order. Neither segment exposes a selected state, which is a separate role-state question outside this finding.
reason: Pay monthly is the selected segment and has tabindex -1 by design, so Tab skips it. The other segment is a tab stop: Enter on Pay annually switches the plans to annual, and in that state Pay monthly becomes the tab stop, so the toggle works both ways from the keyboard.

A full Tab cycle on the API Tokens page (45 stops) covers the token cells and kebab buttons and never lands on Create an API token. That row is a tr with tabindex=-1, no role and no button inside; Enter, Space and the arrow keys on a neighbouring cell open nothing, and the search palette's suggestions show no create-token action. The row is a selectable control in the master-detail table (Debug, LLC and the others open a detail panel on click), and CompConsult's row is disabled (selectDisabled and hoverDisabled classes; click and Enter on its arrow button changed nothing in the screenshots). 1.4.11 covers non-text contrast of active controls and does not apply to an inactive one. No other A or AA criterion covers the colour of this text. Low-vision users may still struggle to read it, which is a best-practice gap, not an AA failure.
reason: The text is the CompConsult account name in the greyed-out 2FA Reset row. value.name: Preferred first name
value.template: textbox "Preferred first name" [invalid=true, errormessage=This field is required]

reason: The Preferred first name input has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing to a real, visible span (This field is required) that sits in no live region, and the accessibility tree exposes errormessage and invalid on the textbox. The red message is on screen and follows the input in reading order, so only AT that ignores aria-errormessage loses the cue at the moment of the error; that weakens 4.1.2 a little and blocks nobody, so low.

The listbox Send to the sweep flagged is a 0x0 position:fixed live region (aria-live=polite, no options) that the combobox uses to announce results, not a control. The real Send to combobox input is reached by Tab (probe via tab, first stop in the modal, ring visible), exposes expanded and haspopup, and ArrowDown opens its menu (aria-expanded true, 21 options), so the task works from the keyboard.

A 48-stop Tab walk on settings.referrals records each stop's document position: the status badges run top to bottom (Applied in the Razer Capital row, then Started in the next row, Pluto Import and Export), matching the DOM and the visual order. The backward jump the sweep read is a scroll artifact: reaching Started scrolls the _layout container by 385px, so its viewport y falls from 878 to 544. Separately, focus drops to the page body about 11ms after landing on Started, so one Tab press shows no focus; that is a focus-loss problem, not a reordering.

The flagged element is the Payout column header: a plain th child div with a pointer cursor and a click handler, no tabindex, no button inside and no aria-sort. Clicking it re-sorts the referral rows (a chevron moves to Payout), but the focus probe cannot reach it (visible: false, via: null) and focus() leaves focus on the body, so keyboard users cannot sort by any column. Every row stays readable, so the task is possible but harder: medium.

Reproduced by keyboard on the Security page: Enter on the second Remove button opens the Remove passkey dialog (role dialog, modal, empty accessible name), Escape closes it, and focus lands on the page body instead of the Remove button, which is still on the page. The next Tab goes to Customize your experience, the first stop, so a keyboard user must tab past about 35 stops to get back, which fails 2.4.3. The task is possible but slow, so it stays medium.

The API Documentation link in the page's second paragraph is #465bd1 on text #1e1e2a (2.88:1 between link and text, AA needs 3:1), with no underline, weight change or border; the underline appears on hover only. Same on both states. The attached contrast probes measure the link against the page background (5.71:1), not against the surrounding text, so they do not test 1.4.1. The link is secondary documentation, not essential text, so it stays medium.

Each token row ends in a menu trigger exposed as button with no name: the ax probes show an empty name on both sampled states, and the snapshot lists three nameless buttons, one per row, each opening Edit and Delete menu items. The Actions column header gives some table context, so it stays medium.

The first row's menu button (an ellipsis icon, svg aria-hidden) has no text, aria-label, labelledby or title: the ax probe reads button with an empty name on both sampled states. No visible text label shares the control (AE3 does not apply). Keyboard focus reaches this inner button, and it opens an Edit and Delete menu, so the task is possible but the control is unidentifiable.

A span role=button tabindex=-1 with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded wraps the native button. Focus lands on the inner button, which exposes no name and no expanded or haspopup state; the state sits on the unfocusable wrapper (ax probes on both states). Screen-reader users get a bare button and are not told the menu is open. That fails 4.1.2, task still possible, so medium.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard is met: the dialog opens from the keyboard alone with Manage (Enter), ArrowDown to the item, Enter, and focus lands in the dialog. Tab not stopping on a role=menuitem with tabindex=-1 is the APG menu pattern, where arrow keys move between items, so no function depends on a mouse. 2.4.3 Focus Order is met: focus goes from Manage to the menu's first item, then to the chosen item, then into the dialog. 4.1.2 is not in question: the item has role menuitem and the name Potentially dangerous action: Unsubscribe.
reason: Tab does skip the menuitem, but it is not a keyboard barrier: on settings.plan-billing, Enter on the Manage button opens the menu and focuses the first item, ArrowDown reaches Potentially dangerous action: Unsubscribe, and Enter opens the confirmation dialog with focus moving into it. The items carry tabindex=-1, as the APG menu pattern prescribes.

It is a legal disclosure reference no task depends on, so the under-2:1 text-contrast line does not make it high and it stays medium.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the WCAG input-purpose list (name, email, address, card number and so on). The GL Code field assigns a general-ledger code to a bank transaction, so it has no listed purpose and 1.3.5 cannot fail. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value is met: the ax probe shows combobox "GL Code" [expanded=false, haspopup=listbox]. No other A or AA criterion covers an autocomplete token on this field.
reason: The GL Code combobox has autocomplete="garbage" next to data-1p-ignore, data-lpignore and data-bwignore, a deliberate autofill opt-out. It picks a chart-of-accounts code for the transaction, not information about the user, and the tree still exposes combobox "GL Code" with its states.

The Check images label is a dt inside a plain div in the drawer section, with no dl ancestor, so the tree exposes a bare term (1.3.1). The two check images keep their own alt text (front of the check, back of the check), so the impact is minor and it stays low.

Reproduced after a click and by keyboard (Tab to the Show transactions for combobox, Space, Escape): Escape closes the unnamed listbox, the combobox stays on the page with aria-expanded false, and focus lands on the body, which fails 2.4.3. criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 requires all functionality to be operable by keyboard. The only control Tab skips is the one for the mode already showing; activating it is a no-op, and switching to line chart by keyboard works from any other mode (Enter on Show overview chart made Show line chart focusable). 2.4.3 focus order stays logical (overview, stacked bar, sankey). 4.1.2 name and role are exposed (button "Show line chart"). That the selected mode is not announced is a different claim from this finding and was not evaluated here.
reason: Reproduced: Tab and Shift+Tab skip Show line chart, because the selected segment has tabindex=-1. But Enter on it changes nothing (same URL and chart), the other three segments are reachable, and once another mode is selected the line button is back in the tab order. Keyboard users lose no function.

Reproduced the Tab from the last Copy section button to the Transactions link on both states. The move is forward, not backward: the link is in the Summary card below the insights block, at page y=1014 against y=690 for the button, and the content area scrolled 570px to bring it into view. criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA) covers messages that report the result of an action, a state change, a warning or an error without taking focus. The page also has a persistent empty role=alert toast container, so a toast would land in a region that already exists, and the table itself is exposed as live=polite. No other A or AA criterion is implicated by this node: the page keeps its Roles heading and table name.

The ax tree shows that table as a live=polite table named Roles, and the page holds an always-present empty role=alert container (id toast-container) where a confirmation toast would render. criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose covers inputs that collect information about the user and match a purpose in the WCAG list (name, email, address, card number and so on). The field's missing name is a 4.1.2 matter covered by name:label:b565c281853a. No other A or AA criterion covers an unrecognised autocomplete token on a non-personal field.

That fails 4.1.2 on both sampled states, and results are silently scoped, so it stays medium.

The results container is a listbox named Google, but its nine li role=option rows sit inside an unroled ul, so the tree exposes them as listitem (probe-ed75692c251a) and the listbox owns no option. aria-activedescendant on the combobox points at a listitem, and aria-selected is lost, so screen-reader users get no option position or selected state while arrowing through results. That fails 4.1.2; the search still works by content, so medium.

The download icon button beside the $1,042.95 amount on the approved-payment page is exposed as button with an empty name: it holds an aria-hidden icon and an empty visually-hidden label span, with no aria-label or title. The page shows no text that does the same thing, so a screen-reader user cannot tell what it does. It fails 4.1.2 on both sampled states; it is not the primary action (Back to Needs Approval is), so it stays medium.

The download icon button next to the PDF file name in the document viewer toolbar is exposed as button with an empty name on both sampled states: an aria-hidden icon, no aria-label, no title. The only way to download the attachment is this button, so a screen-reader user cannot find it. It fails 4.1.2; the payment details are also in text beside the viewer, so it stays medium.

On the Recipients screen the bulk bar wraps each button in a div with tabindex 0, so the first Tab stop on Request tax docs is that wrapper, where Enter and Space do nothing. The next Tab reaches the real button, and Enter opens the Request tax documents dialog with focus inside it, so keyboard users can open it.

Tab onto the Send on field opens the calendar popover on focus alone, so Enter and Space have nothing left to open. The sweep read a popover that was already open as not opened. I did not press Enter in the field because it sits in the payment form.

On Needs Approval, Tab reaches the first row and Enter moves focus to Close detail panel while the panel stays hidden (aria-hidden true, opacity 0, shifted 200px), and Space does nothing, so the detail panel opens only with a mouse click. Ticking the row checkbox with Space and activating Review Request opens the full review page with Approve and Decline, so an equivalent keyboard path exists but is hard to find.

On both parent screens, Tab onto the Name combobox opens the customer list on focus (aria-expanded true, Add new customer and the customer options visible), so there is no separate Enter or Space step. The sweep counted only a list that opened after its keypress.

On Edit Filing the bulk bar wraps Done in a div with tabindex 0, so the first Tab stop is that wrapper, where Enter and Space do nothing. The next Tab reaches the real Done button, and Enter opens the payee drawer with focus on its Close detail panel button, so keyboard users can open it.

On billpay.scheduled and transactions.index, Tab lands on the body of the closed detail drawer, an aria-hidden aside at opacity 0 and off screen, and the focus probe reports it invisible with no ring. The drawer's xpath on transactions.index has moved to /html/body/div[4]/aside[1]/div[1]/div[1] since the sweep; it is the same Loading... panel body. One lost tab stop per drawer, so the task is possible: medium.

Sorting is optional and the rows stay readable, so the task is possible but limited: medium.

On billpay.scheduled and payments.scheduled the closed detail drawer is an aria-hidden aside (ignored in the accessibility tree, opacity 0, shifted 200px off screen) that still holds a focusable Close detail panel button. Focus probes show Tab reaches that button with nothing visible, so focus goes into content screen readers cannot see: it fails 4.1.2 but costs a stop, not the task, so medium.

On both states Choose Files is a hidden file input (tabindex -1, opacity 0.00001, pointer-events none), so no user can see or click it. File upload stays keyboard-operable: Upload attachment is a native button that Tab reaches and Enter makes trigger the input on invoicing.edit-series, and Upload bill on the inbox page is a focusable button whose popover has a file input that Tab reaches.

The Status header is a plain th with no tabindex or role: Tab skips it on both sampled states (focus probes, via null), yet a click sorts the table. No other control sorts the table, so keyboard users lose sorting, but the rows stay readable, so medium.

The Amount header is a plain th with no tabindex or role: Tab skips it on both sampled states (focus probes, via null), yet a click reorders the rows by amount. No other control sorts the table, so keyboard users lose sorting, but the rows stay readable, so medium.

The Last updated header is a plain th with no tabindex or role: Tab skips it on both sampled states (focus probes, via null), yet a click flips its sort indicator to ascending. No other control sorts the table, so keyboard users lose sorting, but the rows stay readable, so medium.

The Needs Approval tab is a div with no tabindex or role: Tab never reaches it on either sampled state, and on /payments ArrowRight, Enter and Space on the focused Inbox tab do nothing, yet a click opens /payments/approvals. These tabs are the only way to the Needs Approval, Scheduled and Paid views (the matching links are display:none and no other page links there), so by AE7 a keyboard user is stuck and it is high.

The red trash button in the first row has an empty label span, no aria-label and no title, so the tree exposes button with an empty name on both sampled states (ax probes). The labeled Delete in the detail panel is another path, but this unnamed destructive button next to Review still fails 4.1.2, and it is not the sole primary action, so medium.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order passes: the popover's content follows its trigger in the tab order and the next control follows the popover, which keeps the sequence meaningful and operable. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence passes: the popover content is in DOM order directly after its trigger. No other A or AA criterion covers where a transient popover is drawn.
reason: On books.home and books.accounts, Tab goes Keyboard shortcuts, then See all shortcuts, then the user menu button. See all shortcuts sits in the shortcuts preview popover that opens under its trigger on focus, so it is the next stop after the trigger, and the user menu is the next control once the popover closes. The 210px rise is the popover's position, not an out-of-order jump.

Payroll Taxes sits directly below Benefits Expense in the Expenses list (page positions 1363 and 1305 px at scroll 0). The sweep read viewport rects, and focusing Payroll Taxes scrolled the page container from 463 to 780 px, so the row's viewport top fell from 842 to 583. The order on the page runs top to bottom.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order passes: Tab completes the Cash card, then the Expenses card, then the Revenue card, the same order a sighted reader follows across the columns. 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence passes: DOM order is column by column, top to bottom within each card. No A or AA criterion requires row-by-row order across independent cards.
reason: Petty Cash is the last row of the Cash card (left column) and View expenses is the first control of the Expenses card (middle column). The page is three side-by-side cards, and Tab finishes one card before it enters the next, left to right. The rise is the move from the bottom of one column to the top of the next.

The Oct 1-31 bar group is at page position 788 px and the Jupiter Checking row at 1129 px, so the row is below the chart, as the screenshot shows. The sweep read viewport rects, and the page container scrolled from 67 to 602 px between the two stops, which made the row look 194px higher.

Salaries and Wages sits directly below Legal in the Expenses list (page positions 957 and 899 px at scroll 0). Focusing Salaries and Wages scrolled the page container from 57 to 436 px, so the row's viewport top fell from 842 to 521. The order on the page runs top to bottom.

Probed again on books.home: Tab reaches the timeline's left scroll chevron (stop 28) and the probe reports it invisible, with no focus change on screen. The button has opacity 0 until the pointer is over the timeline, so its focus ring (a 3px box-shadow) is drawn at zero opacity, and it has no accessible name. Keyboard users can still reach the rest of the page, so it stays medium: the guidance's high case needs a primary-path shared control, and this is a secondary scroll affordance.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard passes: the functionality behind the overlay's click, opening report details for a period, is fully operable from the keyboard through the focusable bar groups (Enter or Space, tested on the Oct 1-31 group). 2.4.3 and 4.1.2 are not at issue for the bar groups, which have names and button roles. The overlay itself carries no function the groups lack.
reason: The unreached element is the transparent plot overlay of the Cash in vs out chart, which opens the period's report on click. Its click handler calls the same callback as the four bar groups, which are role=button with tabindex 0, are reached by Tab (stops 47 to 50), and open the same report panel on Enter or Space. The keyboard path exists, so the overlay is a pointer shortcut.

The rotating placeholder in the search field (Payments over 1.5k, then Documents & Statements) measures 2.68:1 at 16px on both sampled states, where AA needs 4.5:1. It is a hint that cycles through example queries, not the field's only label, so it is not essential text and stays above the 2:1 line for high.

Tab onto the Approvals filter chip draws nothing on either sampled state (diff 0, visible false): the chip sits under the scroll arrow past the strip's edge, and the screenshot shows no ring anywhere in the dialog. Users and Departments are clipped the same way, but search still works by typing, so it stays medium.

On home.search-card-all, pressing Tab in the search field moves focus to the first filter chip and then closes the whole dialog, so neither the chips nor the Scroll filters right button can be reached with a query typed. On home.search-open the arrow is skipped too, but Tab on a chip scrolls the strip so all filters stay reachable, so only the typed state fails; the filters are still usable by picking one before typing, so it stays medium.

The results listbox belongs to a combobox: focus stays in the search field, and ArrowDown and ArrowUp move aria-activedescendant and the highlight through the options (Recent transactions, Scheduled payments, Payment approvals, Cards). The popup is not meant to be a Tab stop, so Tab skipping it blocks no keyboard user.

The listbox's only child is a ul, and Chrome's tree reads listbox, list, then each result as an unnamed listitem [level=1], so the results lose their option role, name and selected state and 1.3.1 fails. Search still works by typing and pressing Enter, so it stays medium.

The plus (zoom in) button in the document viewer toolbar is exposed as button with an empty name on both sampled states: an aria-hidden icon and an empty visually-hidden label span, no aria-label or title. A screen-reader user cannot tell what it does. It fails 4.1.2; the payment details are also in text beside the viewer, so it stays medium.

The Manage link in the Linked profiles row is named only Manage (probe-0b739a9e1867, probe-9cf58f5982f3) and goes to /settings/security. The row label sits in a sibling div, not in a heading, list item, paragraph or table cell, so 2.4.4 context is not programmatic. It is the only link on the page with that text, and the label is next to it in reading order, so the impact is minor.

The country selector beside the phone field is named United States flag, from the flag svg's title, on both sampled states. The name says which country is set but not that the button picks a country code, and it exposes no haspopup or expanded state; the button opens a country list. That is a minor 4.1.2 and 2.4.6 failure: the name is present and the field context makes the purpose guessable.

value.name: Product Search
value.template: combobox "Product Search" [expanded=false, haspopup=listbox, invalid=true, errormessage=Please complete this field]

reason: The Product Search combobox exposes invalid=true and errormessage="Please complete this field" in the accessibility tree, but the message span is not a live region or role=alert and the field has no aria-describedby. Assistive tech that ignores aria-errormessage will not read it on focus, which is a minor 4.1.2 gap in optional ARIA, so low.

The unit price textbox exposes invalid=true and errormessage="Please complete this field", but the message span is not announced by any technique and aria-describedby points to a helptext id that does not exist. The error is visible next to the field and the tree carries it, so the impact is minor 4.1.2 friction in optional ARIA, so low.

After Next is pressed with an empty line item, two "Please complete this field" messages appear in plain spans and divs, outside any live region. The page's only live regions (a status and an alert) stay empty, focus stays on Next, and Next is not aria-disabled, so a screen-reader user hears nothing and does not learn which fields failed. It is not the only confirmation of a money movement, so medium.

On customers-index the pen and invoice icon buttons in each row are exposed as button "", so 4.1.2 still fails. Each row has tabindex=0 and Enter opens a Customer panel with named Edit, Request and Delete buttons, so the same actions have a named path and the failure is friction (AE3). On settings-branding the six theme radios do have names (green-theme, blue-theme and so on), so they are terse, not unnamed, and the white swatch drew white in this build, not dark grey.

Both sampled states show button "": the customers row edit icon, and the trash icon in the Drawdown Recipient panel (the pencil beside it is unnamed too). The customers rows have a named path through the row panel, but the drawdown panel offers no named Delete or Edit, so a screen-reader user cannot tell what these two controls do and the task is hard, not blocked.

Esc closes the Delete Test Person dialog and focus lands on body. Go back does the same, because the detail panel closes with the dialog and its Delete button leaves the DOM. The next Tab goes to the page-end buttons and then wraps, and the first catalog row is about 52 tab stops from the page start, so keyboard users lose their place. The dialog is unnamed (probe) and Go back and Delete item are reachable by Tab, so this is not high.

Reproduced the second verifier live: from a fresh billpay.needs-approval, Tab reaches the Jason Green row at stop 59, and Enter moves focus to Close detail panel while the panel stays aria-hidden at opacity 0. The first verdict saw Enter work only after the panel had been opened once. Ticking the row and using Review Request is an equivalent keyboard path, so medium.

On the sampled state the chip row is scrolled to its end and Scroll filters right is hidden, disabled and ignored by the accessibility tree (probe-831c135ef825), so the measured control is not rendered there. The second verifier's broader point, that Tab closes the search dialog and the chips are mouse-only, is real and stays published through dialog-trigger 4135887522b7 and 4b36722b7bf8 and keyboard a35226f83250.

Same approval panel component as on Bill Pay, where the conductor reproduced it live: a keyboard user's first Enter on the row moves focus to the hidden Close detail panel button and the panel stays hidden. The second verifier saw the same on payments.approval-detail. Review Request from the row checkbox is an equivalent keyboard path, so medium.

Both verifiers probed the same chip (probe-9f179ea0a078: button Transactions, no state) and agree 4.1.2 fails because the selected filter is shown by fill only. The role-state guidance allows low only for optional ARIA or an autocomplete token; a toggle's selected state is not optional, and results are scoped without saying so, so it stays medium.

Same chip pattern as the Transactions chip: both verifiers' probes read button Cards with no pressed or selected state before and after a click. A toggle's selected state is required for 4.1.2, not optional ARIA, so the default medium stands.
Same chip pattern: both probes read button Accounts with no state, and the active filter is conveyed by fill only. A toggle's selected state is required, not optional ARIA, so medium.

Checked live on home.search-results: the listbox labelled by the query (downshift-0-menu) holds li role=option rows inside a ul with no role, and the accessibility tree exposes listbox Google > list > listitem with no option (probe-ed75692c251a). The first verdict's premise that the listbox owns options does not hold, so 4.1.2 fails at medium.

Both probes read button with an empty name for the PDF viewer's download icon on both sampled states. It is the only way to download the attachment, so a screen-reader user can still do it only by guessing at an unnamed button: possible but hard, medium.

Both probes read button with an empty name for the PDF viewer's zoom-in icon, so 4.1.2 fails. Zoom only enlarges the preview for sighted users; the document's text layer and the payment details beside it stay readable to a screen reader, so the unnamed control costs little: low.

Both verifiers' probes read the Customers row icons as button with an empty name, so 4.1.2 still fails. Each row takes focus and Enter opens a Customer panel with named Edit, Request and Delete buttons, so the same actions have a named keyboard path, and the Branding swatches are named (tersely). Friction, low.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 covers messages about success, results, waiting, progress or errors. A newly shown button is a control, not a message, and is named and focusable under 4.1.2. 1.3.1 and 2.4.3 are not affected by it appearing. No other A or AA criterion fails.
reason: Revert changes is a button that appears in the toolbar and the filter panel when a saved view is edited. The ax probe shows button "Revert changes" with a name, so it is a control a screen-reader user finds by navigating, not a message about the result of the amount filter. The unannounced result of the filter change is the transaction count, covered by its own finding.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 covers messages about success, results, waiting, progress or errors. The summary mirrors the input the user entered in controls that expose their own values (textbox At least... holds 150, radio Out is checked). An echo of the user's own input is not a status message. No other A or AA criterion fails.
reason: Money out, ≥ $150 is the filter summary in the panel header (This month, Money out, ≥ $150, Methods (11)). It echoes the value the user just typed in the At least textbox and the Out radio, both visible and exposed in the form beneath it (shot). It repeats the user's input and does not report a result.

Reproduced live: replaying the amount hop from transactions.filter-amount with a mutation observer, the count changed from 68 to 55 Transactions in the footer with no aria-live, status or alert ancestor, and focus stayed in the amount textbox. This is a result count, so 4.1.3 applies. The table is a polite live region (aria-live=polite, aria-busy) that announces the new rows, so users still hear the results, and the task stays possible; the missing count is friction.

Reproduced live: after the amount hop the panel title text changed to Monthly money out (edited) with no live-region ancestor while focus stayed in the textbox. The change tells the user the saved view now differs from the saved version, which is a result of the filter edit, so 4.1.3 applies. The same state is exposed on the chip (menuitem named Editing Monthly money out) and through the Save and Revert changes buttons, so this is minor friction.

criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 covers messages about success, results, waiting, progress or errors. A change in a control's accessible name is not a status message, and the name is correctly exposed under 4.1.2 (menuitem Editing Monthly money out). The user-facing message about the view being edited is covered by the Monthly money out (edited) finding. No other A or AA criterion fails.
reason: Editing is a visually hidden prefix inside the saved-view chip button. It makes the chip's accessible name Editing Monthly money out (ax probe on the chip), so it is part of a control's name and not a message. The same information, that the view was edited, reaches users as the visible (edited) title, covered by its own finding.

The gear icon button beside the forwarding-address chip has an empty label span, no aria-label and no title, so the tree exposes button with an empty name on both sampled states (ax probes). It fails 4.1.2, but it is neither a form control nor the page's primary action, so it stays medium.

The input is a type=file overlay with tabindex=-1 and opacity 0.00001, and the tree gives it only the browser's generic name Choose Files (ax probes), so axe's label finding is real. A labeled button opens the same picker (Upload bill, Upload attachment), so as in AE3 the leftover control fails with minor impact: low.

On both sampled states the closed bill panel is an aside with aria-hidden=true, opacity 0 and pointer-events none, yet it holds 12 tab stops, and Tab goes from the last row's Review straight into them (stops 83 to 94), including an unseen Delete. The task is still possible, but keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place in invisible, silent stops, so medium.

Still true on billpay.index and billpay.row-hover: the row's trash button exposes button with an empty name (ax probes), the four tabs are role-less divs with no name (the Sync Error tab from capture is gone), and the amount input in the opened bill panel is exposed as textbox named 0.00, its placeholder. The task is possible but unclear to screen-reader users, and the labeled Delete in the panel is a partial equivalent, so medium.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 asks for an order that preserves meaning and operability. The order here is sidebar navigation, then page header controls, then page content, and a keyboard user who finishes the sidebar continues at the top of the page, as expected. 1.3.2: the DOM order of the two regions matches their visual reading order (sidebar on the left, page on the right). No other A or AA criterion covers tab order.
reason: On both states Tab runs through the sidebar links, ends on Settings, then moves to the Finalize setup button at the top of the page header and on to Add, Search and the content. Sidebar first, then page, is the layout's order, so the upward move on screen is not a focus-order failure.

The All, Mercury, Bank, Credit, Payments and Payroll filter tabs are plain divs with no role and no tabindex. In 84 Tab presses focus never landed on one, and the tree exposes the Mercury tab as an unnamed generic (probe-7559819ae43e). Keyboard users cannot filter the list by account type, but every account is still listed under All, so no task is blocked.

Tab goes from the last cell of one grid row to the first amount of the next row. With the grid's scroll offset added, the next row sits below the previous one (balance sheet: document y 884 to 920; profit and loss: 1208 to 1316). The grid scrolled about 400px between the two stops, which made the sweep read a rise.

Tab reaches the flagged amount button with its focus ring drawn on both states: 1304 changed pixels on the balance sheet (probe-77fba5bcdfc2, same result on a second run) and 922 on cash flow (probe-633fa14c6cdb), with hidden null. The sweep read clipped at this stop; the button is not clipped when focus arrives.

Focus reaches the flagged amount button but changes 0 pixels on both states (probes probe-28b8645197e9 and probe-68e02f5b9e82): its box runs from x 1328 to 1440, under the frozen Oct MTD column, and the screenshot with it focused shows no ring anywhere. 2.4.7 fails. Keyboard users can keep tabbing, so the task stays possible: medium.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose covers fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose on its list, such as name, email, address or card number. This is a report period picker, not a field about the user, and a token outside the list is the usual way to opt out of autofill. 4.1.2 holds: the input exposes role combobox, a name and its expanded and haspopup states. No other A or AA criterion covers the validity of an autocomplete token.
reason: The Monthly period selector carries autocomplete="garbage" on purpose, next to data-1p-ignore and data-lpignore, to keep password managers out. It is a report-period picker, not a field that collects information about the user.

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose covers fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose on its list, such as name, email, address or card number. This is a report period picker, not a field about the user, and a token outside the list is the usual way to opt out of autofill. 4.1.2 holds: the input exposes role combobox, a name and its expanded and haspopup states. No other A or AA criterion covers the validity of an autocomplete token.
reason: The year selector carries autocomplete="garbage" on purpose, next to data-1p-ignore and data-lpignore, to keep password managers out. It is a report-period picker, not a field that collects information about the user.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 asks for an order that preserves meaning and operability. The order is sidebar navigation, then page header (subtitle status icon, Finalize setup, Add, Search), then content; finishing the sidebar and continuing at the top of the page is expected. 1.3.2: the DOM order matches the visual order of the sidebar and the page. No other A or AA criterion covers tab order.
reason: Tab runs through the sidebar to Settings, then to the Pending close status icon beside the page subtitle, then Finalize setup and Add. Sidebar first, then the page header, is the layout's order, so the move from the sidebar's foot to the top of the page is not a focus-order failure.

criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3: each column's controls stay together and the columns follow in left-to-right order, so the sequence preserves meaning and operability. 1.3.2: the DOM order of Cash, Expenses and Revenue matches their visual order. The scroll back to the top is the browser revealing the focused button. No A or AA criterion fails.
reason: The home page has three columns, Cash, Expenses and Revenue, in that DOM order. Tab from the last Expenses row, Computers and Hardware, goes to View revenue at the top of the Revenue column, and the page scrolls back to the top. Finishing one column and starting the next is column reading order.

Tab goes from Ops / Payroll to Venus Credit Card, the next row of the same list. With the page's scroll offset added, Venus sits 45px below it (document y 1489 to 1534). The page scrolled between the two stops, which made the sweep read a rise.

On both states each result is li role=option in the markup, but Chrome's tree exposes it as an unnamed listitem [level=1] inside a list inside the listbox, so the option role, name and selected state never reach assistive technology and 1.3.1 fails. Search still works by typing and pressing Enter, so it stays medium.

On both states the results ul holds li role=option as direct children, and the tree reads it as a plain list inside the listbox, so axe's list rule fails 1.3.1. It is the same root cause as the aria-required-parent and aria-required-children findings, which carry the user impact, so this one stays low.

Pages is a filter chip inside the search dialog that is already open, not a trigger: the dialog opens from the Search for anything button, which Tab reaches. The real failure is that with a query typed, Tab from the search field focuses the All chip and then closes the dialog, so the Pages chip cannot be reached (2.1.1). Picking the chip before typing works by keyboard (Tab, Tab, Enter, Shift+Tab twice, then type), so it is medium.

With results for Google, the listbox's only child is a ul and Chrome's tree reads listbox, list, then each result as an unnamed listitem [level=1], so the results lose their option role, name and selected state and 1.3.1 fails. Search still works by typing and pressing Enter, so it stays medium.

Tab stop 36 lands on a second Learn more button inside the dual admin toggle's visually hidden label (1px, clipped), and the probe reports hidden clipped with no ring in the screenshot, so 2.4.7 fails. The visible Learn more link is its own Tab stop (34) with a clear ring and the same text, so the cost is one Tab press with no visible focus.

criterionAnalysis: 1.4.3 sets no contrast requirement for text in an inactive user interface component, and these day cells are inactive: real clicks on Oct 11, Oct 12 and Sep 27 or 28 changed nothing on either state, while Oct 13 changed the date. 1.4.11 covers active components and does not apply to inactive ones. No other A or AA criterion sets a color requirement for this text.
reason: The measured text is an unavailable day in the Send on calendar (Oct 11 on payments, Oct 12 on billpay), greyed at 2.68:1. The day is inert: clicking it leaves the date unchanged while clicking an available day (Oct 13) sets it, and its cursor stays the default arrow.

criterionAnalysis: 1.4.3 sets no contrast requirement for text in an inactive user interface component, and the overflow days from the previous month cannot be selected: real clicks on Sep 27 (payments) and Sep 28 (billpay) left the date unchanged, while Oct 13 changed it. 1.4.11 does not apply to inactive components. No other A or AA criterion sets a color requirement for this text.
reason: The measured text is a greyed last-month day in the Send on calendar (Sep 27 on payments, Sep 28 on billpay). It is inert: clicking it changed nothing on either state, while an available day (Oct 13) changed the date.

The Keyword popover is role menu but owns a search field and a Filter for any matching button, which a menu may not contain, so 1.3.1 fails. Tab moves from the trigger into the field, then the button, and the menu is exposed with the name Keyword, so the filter stays usable.

Reproduced. Tab from Match receipts enters the popover (the receipts@mercury.com link), and Escape closes it with focus on the page body instead of the Match receipts button. The file input has no label, so axe fails it, but Chrome exposes it as button "Choose Files", Tab reaches it, and the drop zone draws a focus ring around it. The name is the browser default and does not match the visible text Drag and drop here or click to upload, so the weakness is real but a screen-reader user can still find and use the control.

In the Saved views menu, Tab from the menu lands on the pencil beside Operating expenses, a focusable div with no role or name. Enter and Space do nothing, so the Rename View dialog never opens and only a mouse click opens it. I found no other keyboard path to rename a view, so a keyboard user cannot rename a saved view.

On both states, Esc closes the Category listbox and focus drops to the page body instead of returning to the combobox. The next Tab resumes after the combobox (Add attachment in the row, Clear combobox selection in the panel), so focus is lost from view and the field is skipped. The rest of the page stays reachable, so the impact is low.

criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard passes: the Filters panel is a vertical tablist (role tablist, aria-orientation vertical) with a roving tabindex. Tab stops on the selected tab only, and ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home and End move between tabs and select them, as in the APG tabs pattern, so the Method tab and its panel are operable without a mouse. 4.1.2 passes: each tab exposes role tab, its name, aria-selected and aria-controls. 2.1.2 passes: Tab leaves the panel, the focus probe's walk ended with end: exit. Arrowing onto a tab whose panel has a search field moves focus into that field (a possible 2.4.3 or 3.2.2 issue). That is a different failure from the one claimed here, so I did not rate it.
reason: The Filters panel is a vertical tablist: Tab stops on the selected tab and ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home and End move between tabs, so the Method tab and its panel are reachable by keyboard. The focus probe reached the Method tab through Tab (via: tab), and from a freshly opened panel Tab, Tab, then ArrowDown with a Shift+Tab each time focus jumps into a search field, selects it in 19 key presses (shot). The overlay's real trigger, the Filters (3) button, is a Tab stop in the sweep's own trace. Separate from this claim: arrowing onto a tab whose panel has a search field moves focus into the panel, and after Category it took more than 39 Shift+Tab presses to get back to the tab list.
